#1824. Panama vs Curacao - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joel Lefevre | 13 Nov 2026 15:07

The first semi-finalist in this season’s CONCACAF Nations League will be decided on Sunday, when Panama host Curacao in the second leg of that tie at Estadio Rommel Fernandez in Panama City.

It is all to play for this weekend after these teams drew 0-0 at Ergilio Hato Stadium in Willemstad on Thursday evening.

It was another match full of missed opportunities for Panama on Thursday, who are now without a normal time win in eight successive internationals.

Over that stretch, they have netted a goal or fewer in each game but have not conceded more than one in their last four outings.

Thomas Christiansen’s men have won two of their last three internationals at Estadio Rommel Fernandez and have not lost a Nations League outing at that venue this decade.

This is the first time they go into the second leg of a Nations League quarter-final tie without an advantage, but the Panamanians have never lost at home in this phase of the competition.

Panama have also not lost to a Caribbean side since Jamaica beat them 1-0 in the 2024 Nations League third-place match.

Sunday will mark the second time they welcome Curacao to Panama, with Los Canaleros previously beating them on home soil, 2-1 in 2021.

At times it looked like they were holding on, but to their credit Curacao managed to pull out a result in the opening leg.

That extended their unbeaten run in the Nations League to 10 matches dating back to their promotional campaign in League B in 2024-25.

On Sunday, they can win their first-ever knockout match in this tournament and reach the semi-finals of a CONCACAF competition for the first time since capturing the 2017 Caribbean Cup.

Meanwhile, Dick Advocaat’s team can extend their unbeaten run versus CONCACAF opposition to 13 matches this weekend, with their last defeat against their own region occurring in the 2025 Gold Cup (a 2-1 loss to Honduras).

Curacao boast a 100% record in this competition when netting the opening goal, winning two of their three group matches in that scenario this season.

The Blue Wave have never lost a Nations League match on Central American soil, including a 4-3 comeback win at Costa Rica in this season’s group phase.

On the Panama side, Manuel Moran is still seeking his first caps after being an unused substitute on Thursday, while Cesar Blackman returned to the pitch, coming on for Jorge Gutierrez.

Orlando Mosquera was back between the sticks in the opening leg of this tie after Eddie Roberts got the call in their last friendly versus Ecuador.

At Curacao, we saw four new faces in their starting 11 this week who did not begin their match versus Trinidad and Tobago, including Armando Obispo, Joshua Brenet, Tahith Chong and Ar’jany Martha.

Eloy Room and Leandro Bacuna remain tied for first in all-time caps with the national team as the former collected his second clean sheet of the competition this season.

Mosquera; Murillo, Cordoba, Andrade, Gutierrez; Harvey, Griffith; Carrasquilla, Barcenas, Diaz; Vergara

Room; Sambo, Gaari, Obispo, Carolina; Comenencia, L. Bacuna; Brenet, Margaritha, Gorre; J. Bacuna

While we expect Panama to have the bulk of possession again, they seem to lack that decisive touch in the attacking third, and we believe an in-form Curacao side will hold their nerve in the big moments on Sunday.

#1823. Willie Collum tackles Rangers and Celtic controversies plus Hearts incident that was ‘right on the limit’

SFA head of referees Willie Collum has backed the controversial decision to award Rangers a penalty for a challenge on James Penrice in their 2-0 victory over St Mirren in Paisley last weekend.

Referee Nick Walsh pointed to the spot in the 17th minute of the Scottish Premiership encounter after Penrice went down in the box under a tackle from St Mirren's Samuel Ramos, with Ryan Naderi converting the kick to open the scoring for Rangers.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The decision drew heavy criticism from pundits and former players, with ex-Celtic striker Chris Sutton remarking that Penrice 'played the ref like a piccolo'.

Collum defended the decision on the SFA's VAR Review show, insisting that there was no "clear and obvious error" for VAR to overturn, while admitting that VAR would not have intervened if Walsh had chosen to play on instead.

"The referee is very close to the incident, the best place you could possibly be, and he talks about the player making contact in a tripping motion," Collum explained. "There is contact at the foot level, and particularly higher up the leg at thigh level.

"People will debate about that contact, but the player takes a huge risk. He goes in, challenges for the ball, doesn't touch the ball, and makes contact with the opponent. As soon as the referee blows the whistle here, we fully support this decision.

"You're right to question, 'is there enough contact?' But as soon as this is given on field, there is no doubt for us then the penalty kick is supported.

"I don't think there is a great deal of contact, but there is contact. Also, I don't think the St Mirren player gets close to the ball. He takes a huge risk. Can we say this is not a foul? No.

"When we talk about the bar and setting a threshold, we often talk about VAR intervention and the appropriateness of whether the VAR would get involved. Here, regardless of the onfield decision, when you look at the footage, it is not one that VAR would touch.

"If a referee here plays on, and the on field description is accurate, then we continue the game. But, in terms of refereeing on field, we don't want VAR to re-referee matches, so we need to allow referees to make decisions. What's clear for us here is the referee is very well positioned, the check is then carried out, is there contact, does the communication from the referee match the images we see, and therefore check complete."

When quizzed over the reaction of Penrice possibly exaggerating the contact, Collum added: "Here the level of contact is judged by the referee to be a foul. As soon as he judges that as a foul then we're not really looking at the reaction of the player. The contact for him is enough for a foul, therefore a penalty is correctly awarded."

Penrice was also acquitted over his high-boot challenge on Aberdeen's Afeez Aremu in the Premier Sports Cup semi-final. The Rangers left-back stretched for a ball in midfield and caught the Dons midfielder high on the side and ribs with his studs.

Referee Ryan Lee awarded a free-kick to Aberdeen and opted not to issue any card, describing the challenge as "careless" rather than "reckless", while VAR official John Beaton reviewed the incident but chose not to intervene. Penrice went on to help set up Naderi's winning goal for Rangers.

Collum said: "I was in the VAR centre watching the game and it looked nothing to me on first view. Then when you see the replays you can obviously see there is more to it.

"The referee is caught side-on so he is almost looking through the Aberdeen player when the contact comes. What it's certainly not is careless. The referee describes it as careless, but for us this is a reckless challenge.

"There is an issue here in terms of the height of the challenge, but that's the only criteria for us that's met.

"Lots of media outlets were showing a still image. If you brought the referee to the monitor with a still image of that you would immediately give a red card. But is there excessive force? Is there brutality? For us there is not.

"There is height, but the contact is not forceful, therefore we think it should have been a yellow card."

Collum also examined a challenge by Celtic defender Colby Donovan on Dundee United's Zac Sapsford during the 2-2 draw at Parkhead on October 28.

With Celtic trailing 2-1 moments after United scored twice in quick succession, the 20-year-old right-back lunged into a challenge and caught Sapsford high on the leg. Referee Steven McLean issued a yellow card and VAR official Chris Graham chose not to red card review, allowing Celtic to finish with 11 men and later rescue a point through a Liam Scales equaliser.

Collum argued that the officials got the decision right.

"You can see there is a lot less contact here," he said. "And also the bending of the leg. The leg comes away rather than continuing and extending when the contact is made. It's almost perfect in terms of the process of the check.

"The on field communication clearly add up to what the pictures show and then the VAR team go through it, they know what the referee's description is, they then explain it, they see what the referee is saying is exactly what they are seeing, therefore it is check complete on a yellow card for a reckless challenge.

"Also, I think the retraction of the leg as well. After winning the ball there is contact but he's trying to withdraw to it. You could easily use criteria here on the height. You could say it's high up the leg therefore you could try and justify a red card.

"But we're also not in the business of finding every detail of trying to red card players. We need to make sure that we meet the criteria. Height is one criteria. You heard good use of criteria here. Excessive force? Brutality? Does it meet those requirements? If not, then the onfield decision is fully supported. It's a glancing contact. For us this is more reckless than dangerous."

Hearts, meanwhile, may have been fortunate to avoid a red card for Rogers Mato during their 2-0 victory over Motherwell at Fir Park on October 25 in an incident described by Collum as "right on the limit".

Mato caught Motherwell's Jardell Kanga high on the knee with a follow through on an attempted clearance and Collum admitted that if referee Duncan Nicolson has awarded a red card on field, rather than the yellow card that was given, then VAR would have been expected to uphold the sending off.

"I think this is right on the limit," Collum stated. "We've discussed this with the referees. If the referee had given a red card on the field, check complete for us.

"But the referee gives yellow, he sees it, he describes it, the VAR team look, they don't see that it's excessive force or brutality, and for them there is enough to support the yellow card here.

"We don't want to go finding every detail to start giving red cards. You're right to question about consistency and whatever. But I think this is right on the limit.

"I think if this decision is missed on field and the referee gives nothing there is even more scope for going into a more in-depth check, perhaps around serious foul play."

Collum, however, was ultimately satisfied with the conclusion that was reached by the officials.

"I think there is evidence that this is reckless rather than endangering," he added. "We've also taken time to remind the referees, on-off contact, we need to be careful because there will be times where on-off contact does constitute a red. But what we'd be looking for more to take it to the next level as a categorical red card is a push onto that area of the knee, and a continuation of that. When it is rapid like that, sometimes it's more reckless, than it is red."

#1822. Sheffield Wednesday v Plymouth Argyle: Dave Challinor wants more than silver lining from first real Owls test

When the 51-year-old agreed to become Sheffield Wednesday’s next manager, it was not for nights like last Sunday, when his team went out of the FA Cup at Oldham Athletic in the first round's graveyard slot, suited only to the television companies.

And his maiden game at Hillsborough was a first-team game in little more than name only.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

He watched a team containing at best two or three players who will feature on Saturday lose 4-0 to another League Two side, Accrington Stanley, knowing they were through to the last 32 of the Football League Trophy regardless. Only 5,472 die-hards were there.

Plymouth Argyle, genuine promotion rivals under Bradfordian Tom Cleverley are in town.

At the best of times, when Hi Ho Silver Lining belts out, clapped and sung along to by a crowd of 30,000, it makes the hairs on the back of your neck stand up. When you are experiencing it for the first time as Sheffield Wednesday manager, it must be doubly special.

"I can't wait," says Challinor, whose managerial apprenticeship began in the footballing backwaters of Colwyn Bay and Fylde before progressing to the more established Hartlepool United and Stockport County.

"Even the anthem at the start of the game with, I'm not sure how many were in there on Wednesday but it's still a big noise from behind you (the main stand was the only home section open) with a less than half-empty stadium.

"To be able to experience and witness that at the weekend is something I'm looking forward to.

"It's special, I think, when you go to many football grounds and there's the songs that are sung at the start of games, it provides a special atmosphere.

"For me to be stood there in the home dugout and it be sung by our supporters to our team, makes it that more special.

"It’s something I'm really looking forward to. "

With that comes responsibilities, as Challinor is aware.

Defeat last Sunday was mildly embarrassing, but quickly got over. The midweek loss will barely have registered with some, not at all with others.

But even though history is against him – the Owls have always needed at least a second season to get out of the third tier – Challinor is expected to win promotion from League One this season, so sentiment will quickly turn to anger if his side do not play a lot better than in his first two matches.

"What happens on the pitch after the singing of Hi Ho Silver Lining is going to be imperative," stresses the new manager.

"Straight away, the focus will be on what the game looks like and hopefully putting in a performance that can build momentum and get a run going.

"The challenge that (managing a "big club") brings is something that, for me, personally, was the next thing I need to do for myself.

"The opportunity to come here and be part of something and build something, being part of it, the fanbase, is a great opportunity and one I'm desperate to take."

Even at 3pm on Saturday, it will not be the full-strength Dave Challinor Sheffield Wednesday, with the injury list running into double figures in midweek. Max Lowe, ruled out for four to six weeks with another hamstring problem, is the latest addition.

"We're hoping that Lummers (goalkeeper Joe Lumley) will be back with us really soon, possibly at the weekend," said Challinor that night. "He's done some training with us this week and has ticked off most things.

"He'd be really important because of the experience and the level that he's played at.

"But if that's not the case, Connal (Trueman)'s an able deputy and I'm sure will do a really good job for us.

"Coops (Liam Cooper) trained this week, Billy (Mitchell) and Louie Barry similarly. Th weekend probably comes too soon for Ali (Al-Hamadi). The others, we've got a decision to make.

"It's a massively important game and we want them back. We're just going to make sure we get them back and we keep them back. It can't be a cycle of one comes back, one goes out, one comes back because we never get any stronger."

There could be a change from the back three of the first two matches to accommodate players.

"Potentially," says Challinor. "We'll look at all things in terms of how systems work, how you build and what you do in possession is different to what you do out of possession.

"We need to deal with the threats we're going to be posed. We know what Plymouth will come with.

"They'll be direct, they're aggressive at the top end of the pitch. They want to run behind, they'll put crosses in the box.

"We're going to have to stop crosses. We're going to have to defend our box, but we need to also influence them by getting our players in the right areas of the pitch in order to cause them problems.

"So there'll be a little bit of to-ing and fro-ing, but we'll do whatever we feel gives us the best chance of winning the game."

#1821. What Sebastien Pocognoli said to Billy Gilmour after Scotland miss left him ‘alone on the pitch’

Sebastien Pocognoli has hailed the way Billy Gilmour responded to the horror of missing an open goal just moments after half-time against North Macedonia.

The midfielder experienced a moment to forget when he blazed over from the edge of the six-yard box with the goal gaping in front of him during Friday’s 2-1 Nations League win.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

All’s well that ended well as Scotland kept their Nations League hopes alive thanks to John McGinn’s double. However, there was concern when North Macedonia equalised almost immediately after the midfielder’s opener on 54 minutes.

Gilmour played his part in the recovery before being replaced by Ryan Christie two minutes after McGinn’s winner from the penalty spot. He was given a tremendous ovation by the home crowd, who recognised his bravery in playing through the difficult moments directly after the miss.

Gilmour had to literally pick himself back up from the turf after slumping to the ground following his moment to forget. Pocognoli noted “the noise” as fans sought to process what had happened. He described Gilmour as “alone on the pitch” in this period. But the midfielder did not hide and contributed to Scotland’s win.

McGinn’s second of the night from the spot, after Ben Gannon-Doak was tripped by goalkeeper Stole Dimitrievski, drew the midfielder level with Hughie Gallacher in third place in the all-time Scotland goalscorer standings with 24 goals.

Gilmour, who has scored twice in 51 international appearances, won’t ever feature at the top end of this list but he should now be sitting on three goals for Scotland.

Some have compared his miss to the infamous one suffered by striker Chris Iwelumo in a World Cup qualifier against Norway in 2008.

Peter van Vossen, whose name is forever associated with a horrendous open goal gaffe for Rangers against Celtic in a league fixture 30 years ago this weekend, was also referenced.

“For me, it is part of football to miss big chances,” said Pocognoli. “With his quality, he absolutely has to put it away. It was more difficult to put out!

“But I always say to the players that I am watching the reaction more. I was straight on at him after he missed. I say: ‘Go on!’ He reacted really well and I was really happy.

“That was what I said to him when he came off. I said: ‘Good reaction.’ Because there was a lot of noise after that and he was alone on the pitch. I think he did really well.”

#1820. Why England's Thomas Tuchel is right to talk up Spain 'final'

In reality, it is nothing of the sort. All that will be at stake at kick-off in the Metropolitano Stadium at 7.45pm is who wins Nations League A Group 3, and gets a home second leg in March's quarter-finals, but it makes sense for the coach to big it up.

Because if anything, England find matches between tournaments too easy. They qualified for the last World Cup without conceding a goal, yet found it hard work in America and Mexico.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The Nations League is supposed to match equals, yet they ran out 7-0 winners in Croatia in October. That Thursday's 2-1 win in the reverse game was much tighter was cause for celebration with Tuchel.

"Because we didn't take our chances it was a tight match, which is good overall," he reflected, “because it can't always be glamorous and super-exciting. Sometimes it's about being serious and determined.

"We wanted a final, and on Sunday in Spain we have it."

Tuchel might rest the man he says is still his first-choice goalkeeper, Jordan Pickford, to give Leeds United's James Trafford another chance, slightly undermining his billing of the game.

But Trafford is getting his chance because he is performing so well and other changes will be more likely to strengthen England, with Ezri Konsa and Djed Spence likely to be available after injury and Miles Lewis-Skelly having served a one-match ban.

The narrative around this generation of England players is that they are flat-track bullies, brilliant in qualifying but flaky in finals and semi-finals, or whenever they come up against the world's elite.

World and European champions Spain won 3-2 at Wembley in September, so only need a draw.

They beat England in the last European Championship final, the second in a row the Three Lions had been tamed in. They lost this year's World Cup semi-final to Argentina and started the nearly-men cycle with a last-four defeat to Croatia in 2018.

When they got to the Nations League semi-finals in 2019, poor defending by John Stones and Kyle Walker saw them lose 3-1 to the Netherlands in extra-time.

So no, Sunday is not a "final", a huge occasion, a do-or-die moment for Tuchel's team. But it will not do them any harm to think so.

AC Milan have already discovered the starting price for Nicolo Tresoldi, and it’s safe to say it will not be a cheap deal.

According to this morning’s edition of La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below), it is no secret that Tresoldi sits at the top of the wish list for Milan. Gerry Cardinale, first and foremost, is a big admirer of the rising Brugge star.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It is equally well-known that the striker has been a lifelong fan of the Rossoneri. However, his contract runs until 2029, so to take him away from the Jan Breydel Stadium a negotiation is needed with a club that are tough to deal with, as the past shows.

The phone lines between Milan and Brugge were first used in 2022, when the Charles De Ketelaere saga took place. Since then, the management teams at both Milan and the Belgian club have changed, but the history between the two sides should help facilitate discussions. Ardon Jashari was another arduous negotiation, but one that eventually reached the finish line too.

In the cases of De Ketelaere and Jashari, the pitch has arguably favoured the seller more than the buyer. Perhaps the outcome will be different with Tresoldi, should the two parties actually sit down to negotiate.

One caveat: especially in January, the asking is bound to be significant. How significant? Around €60m, according to whispers from Flanders.

Club Brugge are accustomed to selling their best players when the time comes, but they are under no pressure to do so, especially while the season is still underway. Tresoldi has effectively carried the team on his back, scoring eight goals in the league, five in the Champions League, and one in the Super Cup.

The total: 14 goals in 17 official matches. For the club to part ways with their star striker during the mid-season window – a time when all their competitive objectives remain within reach – the offer would certainly need to be more than substantial.

Furthermore, if the 22-year-old forward maintains his current scoring rate throughout the season, his market value will only continue to climb. It is a risk, but also an opportunity. Moreover, Milan are not alone in the race for Tresoldi.

Bayern Munich and top English clubs are keeping a close eye on the former Hannover man, who was born in Cagliari but is a key player for the German U21 national team. Consequently, if Cardinale wishes to beat the competition, he would need to act quickly and decisively.

#1818. Jair Cunha eyes Brazil start after denying Erling Haaland in Forest win

By Naim Beneddra | 13 Nov 2026 15:17, Last updated: 13 Nov 2026 15:17

Nottingham Forest defender Jair Cunha could be handed another Brazil start under Carlo Ancelotti just days after producing a remarkable performance against Erling Haaland and Manchester City in the Premier League.

The 21-year-old Brazilian has emerged as one of the most encouraging stories of Forest's difficult start to the season, establishing himself in Oliver Glasner's defence after struggling for opportunities during his first year in England.

His progress was underlined last Saturday when he scored the opening goal in Forest's 3-1 victory over Manchester City before producing a crucial goal-line clearance to deny Haaland.

Now, with Paris Saint-Germain captain Marquinhos absent through injury, Cunha is competing for a place alongside Arsenal's Gabriel Magalhaes in Ancelotti's starting XI for Brazil's friendly against Japan on Saturday.

The Nottingham Forest youngster faces competition from Manchester City defender Vitor Reis, but his recent performances have strengthened his case for another opportunity on the international stage.

Cunha's emergence has been particularly impressive considering how slowly his Premier League career began.

Forest signed the central defender from Botafogo in July 2025, handing him a five-year contract after he had impressed at the Club World Cup.

Previously developed by Santos, Cunha arrived in England with considerable promise, having also helped Brazil win the South American Under-20 Championship.

However, his first campaign at the City Ground proved challenging.

The Brazilian struggled to establish himself amid repeated managerial changes, making only three senior appearances by the end of February 2026.

He also spent time with Forest's Under-21 side while adapting to English football, before gradually receiving more opportunities during the closing months of the season.

The arrival of Glasner and another pre-season in England have helped accelerate his development.

Cunha has established himself as a regular option in Forest's three-man defence, alongside fellow Brazilian Murillo and experienced Serbian international Nikola Milenkovic.

His emergence is particularly noteworthy given the competition for places, with Forest having also invested approximately €40m (£35m) in the signing of Ousmane Diomande.

Although Glasner's side have struggled for consistency, Cunha has demonstrated the combination of physical presence, pace and composure in possession that initially attracted Forest to him.

Those attributes were evident in the victory over Manchester City on November 7.

After just six minutes, Cunha pressed high up the pitch, dispossessed Josko Gvardiol and drove into the penalty area before beating Gianluigi Donnarumma.

It was the defender's first goal for Forest and helped lay the foundations for a memorable victory, with Liam Delap subsequently scoring twice against his former club.

Yet Cunha's most important defensive contribution came shortly before half time.

Haaland had rounded goalkeeper Matz Sels and appeared set to score, only for the Brazilian to recover and clear the Norwegian's effort off the line.

The intervention preserved Forest's two-goal advantage and provided another illustration of the youngster's growing confidence at Premier League level.

Cunha's improvement has already earned recognition from Ancelotti, who included him in his Brazil squad for the September and October international fixtures.

The defender made his senior debut against Australia and collected three caps during that international period.

He started the second meeting with Australia, completing 69 accurate passes and recording 78 touches, while impressing with his ability to track opposing forwards and cover space behind the defensive line.

Those qualities could prove useful as Ancelotti continues assessing his options in central defence.

Marquinhos remains an established figure in the national team, but his absence from the current squad has created an opportunity for younger defenders to impress.

Gabriel Magalhaes is among the leading candidates to start against Japan, leaving Cunha and Vitor Reis competing to partner the Arsenal centre-back.

Cruzeiro defender Jonathan Jesus is another option in the squad, while Arthur Dias offers additional cover.

Cunha's familiarity with the demands of Premier League football could work in his favour, particularly after his performance against one of the competition's most dangerous forwards.

However, his inclusion in the squad preceded the Manchester City victory, meaning the display against Haaland should be viewed as further evidence of his progress rather than the reason for his international selection.

Ancelotti has also indicated that the November fixtures will bring the current period of experimentation to a close, increasing the importance of opportunities for players hoping to establish themselves in his longer-term plans.

Brazil face Japan at Singapore's National Stadium on Saturday before meeting the hosts on November 17.

Cunha is already being considered for a starting role, with Sports Mole's predicted Brazil lineup against Japan placing him alongside Gabriel in central defence.

Whether Ancelotti selects him or opts for Reis remains to be seen, but the contrast with his situation at Forest earlier this year is striking.

A defender who was struggling for regular first-team football just months ago is now pushing for a place in Brazil's starting XI, having delivered arguably his finest Premier League performance against Manchester City.

#1817. Newcastle’s limitations exposed by Bournemouth before hosts fight back for draw

This was the definition of a hard-earned point. Newcastle United came back from two goals down to rescue a point against Bournemouth, but this was not a convincing performance from Matthias Jaissle’s side.

Newcastle were abject for the first half an hour and the visitors could have been out of sight. It was disjointed and lacklustre as Bournemouth dominated before the break and regularly threatened Lukasz Hornicek in goal.

Even during the fightback, Newcastle lacked cohesion and penetration, but forced their way back into it through hard work, spirit and determination. Whether you believe Harvey Barnes’ wonder goal and Jacob Ramsey’s late strike paper over the cracks or reveal a togetherness – a grit and determination that bodes well for the future – depends on the individual.

Ramsey comes off the bench to fire Newcastle level! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UBWAfCQyy4

For the second weekend in a row, Newcastle had just two shots on target and scored two goals. At the other end of the pitch, they have allowed their opponents 61 shots in just three games, the highest in the division. That is not going to be sustainable long term. Something Jaissle acknowledged.

“It shows where we have potential,” he said. “There are elements to improve offensively.

“The learning curve is there. There were some elements missing from our performance but there was a strong response. The lads showed big character, big personality and big commitment... It is always better to get a point and see the potential to improve.”

A reality check is not necessarily a bad thing. There has been a lot of hype and excitement on Tyneside and a self-congratulating tone to their own end of summer appraisals.

But this was a reminder of the team’s limitations and the fact that only three of their eight summer signings started the game, with two more coming off the bench, underlined they are a work in progress.

In truth, that is fine. It is the start of September and the Premier League campaign is only three games old. They have a new manager and a new-look team. There has been a significant amount of change in a very short period of time.

It was not the easiest summer, and despite the insistence from senior figures at the club that they had always remained calm and methodical during their summer reset, there was a whiff of crisis only a few weeks ago.

When Eddie Howe quit as manager and Bruno Guimarães, the captain, forced his move to Arsenal at the start of August, Newcastle looked in disarray. So, to have started the season unbeaten from three games against Liverpool, Tottenham Hotspur and Bournemouth is encouraging.

It is also worth highlighting just how good the visitors were. In the first half Bournemouth were superb, rushing Newcastle, forcing mistakes and pouring forward in numbers. In Alex Scott, just as he was in their victory here last season, Bournemouth had the best player on the pitch.

That opens up another conversation. Newcastle played like this a lot at home in Howe’s final season in charge, especially in the second-half of the campaign, but tended to lose not draw the game.

On this occasion, they secured a decent point with a late equaliser thanks to substitute Ramsey, who looked good when he replaced the off-colour Lewis Miley.

Bournemouth will feel they should have held on. They had taken a deserved lead through Marcus Tavernier, who took advantage of a static and ball-watching Amar Dedić to bundle home from close range.

Tavernier gives Bournemouth the lead at St James' Park! 🍒🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/mDdb5uV4hj

Marco Rose’s side should have scored again minutes later when Sven Botman gifted the ball to Evanilson on the edge of the Newcastle area, but he failed to hit the target.

Bournemouth had their tails up and when another blunder from Dedic – galloping forward and losing possession with a heavy touch – Nico González, another new signing, failed to make a tackle to stop the attack.

Justin Kluivert’s long-range strike thumped against the post and hit the back of goalkeeper Lukasz Hornicek. Scott reacted quickest and his cross spun into his own net off the leg of Malick Thiaw.

Bournemouth have a second and St James' Park is stunned! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Kyy91awf39

Newcastle were in disarray and were lucky to be back in the game before half-time as Barnes whipped in a stunning strike 25 seconds after the restart.

Bournemouth have a second and St James' Park is stunned! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Kyy91awf39

Despite seeing more of the ball, other than a Joe Willock header that dropped wide of the post early in the second half, Newcastle did not create another clear goal-scoring opportunity until Ramsey’s equaliser.

That is a cause for concern, but Newcastle remain unbeaten. Nothing shapes perceptions more than results. Jaissle is right to cling to the positives from that.

Speaking to TNT Sports, the Newcastle boss said: “Mixed feelings. Happy for that spirit, that belief the lads were showing until the end together with the crowd. I felt the energy and felt if we had five or 10 minutes more we could win this game. But the first half was not expected. This is something we need to improve. This is part of the journey.

“We knew Bournemouth would come with everything, they always show great intensity and if you do not compete with that you get problems. We struggled with that in the first half but the lads showed the right reaction.”

"I'm really happy with the confidence the lads brought onto the pitch today." 👏Marco Rose reflects on Bournemouth's performance after taking a point at St James' Park.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/GULqEAUSbx

3 - Bournemouth are the first team in Premier League history to score the opening goal in their first three games of a season and fail to win any of them (D2 L1).Fragile. pic.twitter.com/8mBbabT0VV

"Since the new manager's come in, all the attacking players have had meetings before the game." 👀Jacob Ramsey reveals how Matthias Jaissle is working with Newcastle's attacking players.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/m7lyG29MlE

It’s all over at St James’ Park. Newcastle come from two goals down to salvage a hard-fought point against Bournemouth. For the third Premier League game running, Rose’s side have dropped points from a winning position by conceding a late goal, while the hosts’ unbeaten start to the season continues. On the balance of play, a draw is a fair reflection. Both sides really gave it everything.

Jacob Ramsey grabs a late equaliser to complete a Newcastle comeback against Bournemouth pic.twitter.com/qb5i4oaBO9

Dedic takes the free-kick and curls it over the bar from a long way out. Bournemouth make a very late change as Scott is off for Christie.

Smith clatters into Barnes for a late booking. It’s wave after wave of Newcastle pressure at the moment as Barnes wins a free-kick against Cook.

The noise inside St James’ Park is incredible. The home fans are roaring on the Newcastle players to find a third goal. Bournemouth look absolutely exhausted.

Amid the late drama, Bournemouth make another two changes as Gannon-Doak and Jebbison replace Tavernier and Rayan. There will be six minutes of added time. Can either side find a late winner?

Bournemouth fail to deal with a looped cross into their penalty area and can’t clear the danger. Barnes’ initial effort is blocked and the ball breaks to Ramsey, who slams a clinical low strike into the bottom corner to send the Newcastle fans wild. The hosts from come from two goals down, but can they go on and win it now?

Ramsey comes off the bench to fire Newcastle level! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UBWAfCQyy4

Murphy does brilliantly to beat Truffert to the ball and drive down the wing. The Bournemouth defender has a hold of his shirt and is booked.

Scott rolls a short free-kick into Tavernier, who is allowed to carry the ball to the edge of Newcastle’s penalty area. After a few touches, he shoots, but his thunderous effort comfortably flies off target.

The current state of the game suits Bournemouth. There’s been a lot of fouls from both sides, halting the rhythm. It’s been very stop-start in this second half.

Safe to say that the Newcastle fans are not happy with the referee. Fernandez-Pardo stands on Smith, giving Bournemouth a free-kick. The home support loudly boo the decision.

Newcastle respond with another double substitution. Steur and Murphy are on, with Nico and Elanga departing the action.

The pace of this game has slowed down in the last 15 minutes, with both sides starting to look really tired. Bournemouth then make two changes as Cook and Brooks replace Adams and Kluivert.

Jaissle is booked for breaching his technical area while appealing a refereeing decision. Bournemouth are sinking deeper and deeper as they try and hold on to their slender advantage.

Fernandez-Pardo has been tasked with unlocking Bournemouth’s defence in this closely-fought encounter, but is still waiting for his moment.

Kluivert hauls new signing Fernandez-Pardo and is given a yellow card, prompting cheers from the Newcastle fans.

It looks like Fernandez-Pardo will slot into the No.10 position behind Wissa as Newcastle continue their search for an equaliser. Bournemouth are defending well as a unit in this second half.

Newcastle’s double-change is here as Fernandez-Pardo comes on for his debut, replacing Willock. The other alteration sees Ramsey come on for Miley.

Newcastle have been the more aggressive side since the restart. Hall cuts inside and after receiving a short corner and shoots, but his effort is high and wide. Fernandez-Pardo and Ramsey look like they’re stepping up their respective warm-ups as they prepare to enter the action.

Wissa is booked for unceremoniously barging Adams in an off-the-ball collision. Jaissle can’t believe it and passionately demonstrates his frustration towards the referee and fourth official.

Just like the first half, there’s also been a fast start to the second. Both managers are still pacing up and down their technical areas.

Newcastle are so close to a leveller! Wissa drives forward from inside Newcastle’s half, then dribbles away from Scott, before skipping past Silva. He manufactures some space and clips a pinpoint cross into Willock, who glances a header agonisingly wide of the far post. That was brilliant play from Wissa.

Newcastle get in behind Bournemouth’s backline as Willock latches onto Hall’s through ball. The former Arsenal academy graduate plays in Barnes, whose one-on-one attempt is smothered by Petrovic. The offside flag was then raised against the Newcastle attacker.

We are back under way for the second half. Here we go again.

Three @premierleague games ✅Two @premierleague goals ✅ pic.twitter.com/B46guzqUjm

A thrilling first half comes to a close. What a fantastic game of football so far. Bournemouth flew into a two-goal lead through Tavernier’s composed finish and Thiaw’s own goal, before Newcastle pulled one back thanks to Barnes’ superb strike. The visitors are in front, but it’s still all to play for at St James’ Park.

Two goals in two minutes leaves it intriguingly poisedIt's Newcastle 1-2 Bournemouth at half-time pic.twitter.com/iqTsAKRuVF

There will be three minutes of added time to finish off this breathless first half. Can Newcastle find a late leveller before the break or will Bournemouth restore their two-goal advantage?

It’s end-to-end at St James’ Park. This game is being played like a basketball match. Both teams are flying forward in numbers at every opportunity.

Oh dear not a great moment for two of Newcastle’s summer signings as Bournemouth extend their lead. Amar Dedic lost the ball with a heavy touch and Nico Gonzalez’s half hearted tackle failed to halt Bournenouth’s counter attack.

There was misfortune after with the ball spinning into his own net off Malick Thiaw but Newcastle have been abject.

Thankfully for their manager and supporters, Harvey Barnes’ wonder strike, out of nothing, has got them back into a game they have looked second best in every area of the pitch so far.

What a goal! 27 seconds after the kick-off, Barnes darts inside of Adams and curls an incredible effort into the top corner. Newcastle are back in it and St James’ Park is alive again.

Barnes provides an immediate response for Newcastle, what a hit! 🚀📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/eIhwkvoMl0

St James’ Park cannot believe it. Kluivert tries his luck from range and his whipped effort strikes the post. Scott follows up and attempts to tee up Evanilson with a cross. It takes a wicked deflection off Thiaw and loops over Hornicek for an own-goal. Bournemouth are in dreamland.

Bournemouth have a second and St James' Park is stunned! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Kyy91awf39

Running the risk of sounding like a broken record but Scott is running the show in midfield. Tavernier has also made a very effective start and scored the opener via a brilliantly-taken opener. Truffert has also produced a magnificent, well-rounded display in defence and attack so far.

Newcastle have been very, very poor. Bournemouth have been excellent. As they have tended to be on their trips to St James’ Park.

Newcastle cannot build any cohesion or momentum in the game. They look disjointed and disorganised. Bournemouth have had ten shots compared to Newcastle’s one.

Easily the worst half an hour of Matthias Jaissle’s short time in charge and as bad as anything we have seen from Newcastle in front of their own supporters for a while.

Bournemouth’s high press works again and the ball breaks loose to Kluivert. He shoots from range and his deflected strike flies narrowly wide of the post.

Elanga’s frustrating afternoon continues as he collides with Silva as both players compete for the ball. The Newcastle winger picks up the game’s first yellow card because of the challenge.

The away side storm forward on the counter as Scott finds Truffert with a piercing pass. The Bournemouth left-back exploits the space vacated by Dedic. Truffert picks out Tavernier with a low cross, but the Englishman’s tame effort is saved by Hornicek. You would expect a lot more from Tavernier there, but Bournemouth look so dangerous going forward.

Bournemouth defend a couple of Newcastle corners in quick succession. The hosts are yet to create a notable chance.

There’s a real intensity to this game. Bournemouth are attempting to match Newcastle’s pace and physicality in every department. Just now, there was a really interesting battle between Willock and Adams, with the Newcastle man eventually winning a free-kick after a strong dribble.

Bournemouth look to have found a rhythm, with Scott dictating proceedings from the centre of the pitch. Truffert has done well early on to deal with Elanga’s attacking threat.

Bournemouth have taken the lead and Newcastle United supporters and [players are furious. Referee Rob Jones appeared to miss a pretty blatant shirt tug from Adrien Truffert stopping Anthony Elanga from spinning away, but that does not excuse the weak defending that led to the visitors scoring moments later.

Lewis Hall was beaten too easily by Rayan whose cross was only half cleared by Malick Thiaw but Amad Dedic got caught ball watching allowing Marcus Tavernier to steal in at the far post to bundle in a deflected shot from Evanilson.

Bournemouth should be two in front. A terrible pass from Sven Botman gifted the Brazilian the ball on the edge of the Newcastle box but he failed to hit the target.

Newcastle are rattled. They have not got to grips with Bournemouth in midfield and they are crowding out Yoane Wissa and Joe Willock whenever Matthias Jaissle’s side look to go direct.

We wondered how Newcastle would match up against Bournemouth and they have looked second best so far.

What a chance for Bournemouth to double their lead! What is Botman doing? The centre-back misplaces a pass and Evanilson latches onto the mistake. The striker runs in on goal, but blazes the glaring opportunity over the bar. That’s a huge let-off for Newcastle. Evanilson must do better from that range.

Scott’s deflected strike richochets into Tavernier’s path, with the Bournemouth attacker sneaking in behind Dedic, who switches off. Tavernier then directs a half-volley into the roof of the net. Newcastle are furious. They feel they should of been awarded a free-kick after a earlier tussle between Truffert and Elanga. Both players are pulling each other’s shirts. After a quick VAR check, the goal stands and the away fans are delighted.

Tavernier gives Bournemouth the lead at St James' Park! 🍒🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/mDdb5uV4hj

Dedic shows his quality by intercepting a pass from deep, skipping away from Scott’s sliding challenge and then dribbling all the way to the byline. He can’t quite win a corner, but his efforts are appreciated by the Newcastle faithful.

Newcastle attempt to counter through Wissa and Willock, with the latter passing to Barnes. However, the former Leicester man cuts inside and runs into trouble, causing the opening to disappear.

Tavernier takes it and fires a low effort around the wall, but Hornicek is there to get down low and make a relatively routine save.

Elanga has made a busy start to this game. The winger’s pace is so explosive. Bournemouth then win a free-kick on the edge of Newcastle’s penalty area as Miley catches Kluivert. Mulitple Bournemouth players are standing over this.

The visitors get us under way at St James’ Park. Which German manager will prevail?

Newcastle are in their iconic black and white strip, while Bournemouth are sporting an eye-catching purple away kit. We are just minutes away from kick-off. St James’ Park is in full voice.

An unchanged line up for Newcastle United in Matthias Jaissle’s third Premier League game as manager but this is a very different sort of challenge.

Despite having a miserable record against Bournemouth in recent years, Newcastle will be expected to win this afternoon. The atmosphere, electric for the opener against Liverpool and the return of villain Alexander Isak, will be more expectant today.

These are the fixtures Eddie Howe’s team repeatedly slipped up in at home last season, where the likes of Everton, Brentford, Bournemouth and Sunderland all won.

Can Jaissle improve that record? Can his team thrive when they are likely to have more of the ball, play against a low block defence and an opponent adept at lightning-fast counterattacks?

Does the German’s “vertical” football have as much success against a team that does not play a high defensive line as Liverpool and Tottenham did?

We are likely to know a lot more about Newcastle after this game. There has been a lot of hype and excitement after an impressive start to the new season but have people got a little carried away?

Let’s see how they get on against a Bournemouth side that probably should have got at least a point away to Manchester City in their opening away game.

The talented 23-year-old was the subject of interest from the likes of Arsenal, Manchester United and Chelsea in the summer, but Bournemouth managed to keep a hold of him, despite the midfielder rejecting the opportunity to sign a new contract at the club.

With his current deal expiring in 2028, Scott has made an excellent start to this season, and scored a brilliant opener in Bournemouth’s 1-1 draw with Everton last weekend.

When Newcastle United’s recruitment team finalised their list of priority targets in the spring, Matías Fernandez-Pardo featured prominently.

There was excitement about what he could bring to the team. There was a buzz of possibility. The 21-year-old forward had impressed everyone, from scouts to decision-makers. The call to make him one of their first-choice targets, alongside Switzerland international Johan Manzambi, was unanimous. Just as it had been when Newcastle identified Alexander Isak as their leading target in the summer of 2022.

These meetings are a place for ideas to be shared and different targets pushed. Everyone had their own opinion and various favourites, but Fernandez-Pardo was, in the words of one member of Newcastle’s recruitment team, “the one”.

Unsurprisingly, Matthias Jaissle has named the same starting 11 that beat Tottenham last time out. New signing Matías Fernandez-Pardo is among the substitutes and could make his Premier League debut here.

Good morning and welcome to our live coverage of this Saturday lunchtime fixture between Newcastle United and Bournemouth at St James’ Park.

The hosts have made a determined start to the 2025-26 season under new head coach Matthias Jaissle. They conceded a last-minute penalty to draw 2-2 with Liverpool on the opening weekend of the Premier League campaign, sealed a hard-fought 3-2 victory over West Bromwich Albion in the Carabao Cup, and then produced an inspired second-half performance to win 2-0 away at Tottenham in their previous top-flight outing.

Despite anxiety in the summer after losing Eddie Howe and multiple key players such as Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimaraes and Anthony Gordon, the Jaissle era has begun very encouragingly. New signings including Lukas Hornicek, Amar Dedic and Nico Gonzalez have seamlessly slotted into the starting XI, Lewis Hall has been typically brilliant, while Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa look reborn up top after both forwards endured difficult campaigns last season.

Marco Rose’s Bournemouth tenure has started in frustrating circumstances. They had been leading 1-0 against Manchester City in their first top-flight fixture this campaign, but conceded two late goals to dramatically lose 2-1. Bournemouth were also left kicking themselves last weekend against Everton, after a defensive mix-up between Ryan Christie and Marcus Tavernier following a corner delivery gifted James Tarkowski a 91st-minute equaliser, allowing the visitors to salvage a 1-1 draw at the Vitality Stadium.

At opposite ends of the country, over 350 miles separate these two sides. Away days in English football can’t really get any longer. The travelling Bournemouth support will hope their loyalty can be repaid with a first Premier League win of the season under Rose, while Newcastle will aim to continue their unbeaten start and carry on the positive momentum created by Jaissle.

Kick-off is at 12:30, with team news coming shortly.

#1816. Harry Kane on the inspiration to keep on shining for England

Thursday night at Wembley was not about England v Croatia, not really. It was not particularly about the Nations League, where the hosts needed to avoid a seven-goal defeat to be sure of going through to the quarter-finals (ooh the jeopardy!). It was all about Kane.

England's captain was greeted with a huge tifo as he led his team out of the tunnel for the 98th time.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Before the anthems and handshakes he broke from the line to pick his Ballon d'Or trophy off a plinth, and be presented with a framed shirt to mark his 126th appearance for the Three Lions, a new record.

Luka Modric handed him a replica of Croatia's oldest preserved football, brought to Zupanja by English industrialists in 1880.

It was a nice touch between two teams who have got to know each other rather well in the 21st Century, and two players who were team-mates at Tottenham Hotspur.

Modric is 41 years-old, eight years his senior. When he was 33, Modric also won the Ballon d'Or but it has not sated his appetite.

He was only a substitute when he won his 207th Croatia cap on Thursday, but it was telling he was given a warm ovation when he came off the bench in the second half with the game still in the balance.

Few opposing players get that at Wembley, and it was in stark contrast to the reception afforded to former Leeds United loanee Ben White when he came off the home bench two minutes later. He has not been forgiven for abandoning the ship at the 2022 winter World Cup.

Modric plays his club football at AC Milan, where there is a proud history of elderly players thriving, and has contributed nearly 750 Serie A minutes already this season.

Kane seems to be getting better, a more rounded player with every year of his 30s.

His part in the first goal was a case in point. The younger Kane did not often drop deep and play passes of the quality that released Jude Bellingham to set up Morgan Rogers for England's opener in the 2-1 win, but the 2026 version spends more time away from the frontline than on it.

"That's an area of the pitch I like to play in, that kind of left pocket," he explained. "The more I play with the guys, the more of a relationship I build up with Jude and Morgan and Trent (Alexander-Arnold, selected at right-back), whoever's playing, they know when I'm in that position, I'm probably going to play that type of ball, so they make the runs.

"It's just a pass that's a big strength of mine. It's something I've practised a lot when I was young and still do. You've seen over recent years, especially, that it's been a big weapon."

To carry on as long as Modric is a big ask but Kane has plenty of incentive to go on a couple more years yet.

His penalty to win the game five minutes after sloppy England set-piece defending brought Croatia back into it with a Petar Sucic strike was his 92nd goal for his country.

Only three other players – Cristiano Ronaldo, Lionel Messi and Iran's Ali Daei – have hit 100 in international football but there was no dodging the question when he was asked if it was possible: "I think it's achievable for sure."

And with the talent around him, leading his team onto the winner's podium at the 2028 European Championship final at Wembley, after consecutive losing finals, looks realistic too.

"If we win a major tournament, which is my ultimate goal, the celebrations not just inside the stadium, will be incredible," he said.

Seeing someone like you achieve what you want to is perhaps the biggest motivation of all.

"He's an inspiration for all of us," marvelled Kane when asked about Modric. "What an incredible player, what a great person as well, and someone who's looked after himself, a great professional.

"To be playing at 41 now, still at this level, is a credit to all of his hard work and his mentality. That inspires me to push to the limits.

"I think you just keep going to see how far your body takes you, your mentality takes you.

"As long as I feel like I can help the national team, as long as I feel like I'm performing at the highest level, I'll be here. Whether that's until I'm 40 we'll have to wait and see.

Thursday was just about celebrating one of the England greats and having failed to score and even missed a penalty since being crowned European football’s best player, he did not disappoint.

"It's demanding to get all the recognition, all the prizes, all the acknowledgement,” said Kane’s coach, Thomas Tuchel. “The gentleman he is, he responds to everything.

"It would be easy to lose focus, which he obviously never does.

"We were determined to get this result on his special evening. That he got it in the end with a decisive penalty makes it even more perfect.”

England won 7-0 in Croatia in October. Kane made Thursday top it.

#1815. I watched Scotland’s World Cup games in the pub - but 142-day whirlwind has me primed to make Hampden impact

From watching the World Cup from the comfort of his local pub to making his first international start at the heart of Scotland’s defence, it’s been a remarkable couple of months for Luke Graham.

Nominated for the SWFA Young Player of the Year award following a series of colossal displays for Dundee last season, many tipped him to make a late claim for a place in Steve Clarke’s squad for the tournament in the summer. Despite coming close to making the final 26-man list, there was no seat on the plane for Graham.

Courted by both Celtic and Rangers in the weeks that followed, Portsmouth had launched a seven-figure bid during the January window. However, when the summer transfer window re-opened, it was Stoke City who won the race for his signature. Currently third in the EFL Championship, Graham has been a star performer for them this season.

Awarded his first international start in Friday’s 2-1 win over North Macedonia, Graham admits things are beginning to fall into place. “Not much is going wrong for me at the moment,” he smiled. “I wouldn’t say I merited a start, we have a lot of good players in the camp. It’s up to the manager to pick the team and, luckily, he gave me the chance.

“I have to be ready for it. It’s something I’ve always wanted to do since I was growing up. It was a dream come true. I’ve always said that one thing I wanted to do in my career was play for Scotland, so to get it over the line was pretty special. I had my mum, my dad, my sister here and quite a few of my mates. A good turn out.

“We have a lot of good centre-halves. Obviously it was unfortunate for Welshy [Stephen Welsh] and Binksy [Luis Binks] to go out with injury but that opens up a space for me to come in and try to cement a place. When you’re out on that pitch, you have to do everything you can to try and stay in the team. I gave my all and I’ll just need to wait and see what happens.

“We’re going through a bit of a transitional spell just at the minute, so it’s not going to be all smooth sailing from the get-go. It’s about adjusting to that and try to build on performances in every game.”

It was all so different for the youngster a mere 142 days ago. Asked how he digested Scotland’s World Cup adventure - the first in his lifetime - during the summer, Graham’s financial situation stopped him from attending the tournament in North America. However, on the evidence of his composed performance against North Macedonia, he’s got every reason to believe he won’t need to watch from afar when Scotland next travel to a major tournament.

“I didn’t go [to the World Cup] - it was too expensive for me!” laughed Graham. “I was just like everyone else, watching in the pub with their mates. It was pretty amazing and hopefully I can be part of something like that one day. I wasn’t too far away, Steve Clarke told me. It’s just about trusting myself now and hopefully get there one day.”

#1814. Carlo Ancelotti reveals Brazil selection deadline for five youngsters

By Naim Beneddra | 13 Nov 2026 15:41

Carlo Ancelotti has confirmed that Brazil's period of experimentation will effectively come to an end after November's international break, placing greater significance on the opportunities available to five uncapped youngsters.

The five-time world champions are preparing to face Japan on Saturday before taking on Singapore next Tuesday, with Ancelotti using the final two fixtures of 2026 to assess players who could feature in his plans for the 2028 Copa America and 2030 World Cup.

Manchester City winger Allan, Cruzeiro defender Jonathan Jesus, Corinthians midfielder Andre Luiz and Shakhtar Donetsk pair Marlon Gomes and Alisson Santana are all hoping to make their senior international debuts.

Their inclusion follows Brazil's disappointing last-16 elimination against Norway at the 2026 World Cup, which prompted Ancelotti to accelerate the development of a new generation.

However, the Italian has now indicated that the time for widespread changes is running out, with a more settled squad expected when Brazil reconvene in March 2027.

Speaking at a press conference in Singapore on Friday, Ancelotti explained that he had gathered sufficient information from the international windows since the World Cup to begin narrowing his options.

"This period of experimentation will end during this international break. Next time, we will narrow down the squad a little more," Ancelotti told reporters, as quoted by ge.globo.

"It has been a period that has given us a lot of information about the young players. We know we have youngsters with a lot of talent who are very committed, and that gives us confidence for the future.

"We have players of a very high level. We have cover in some positions, a little less in others, but we have time."

The former Real Madrid manager also suggested that the core of his future squad was already taking shape, although he left the door open for players currently outside the national team.

"There are some players we have looked at who are not here and could be involved next time, but there aren't many. The squad is more or less settled," he added.

Brazil's rebuilding process began in September, when Ancelotti selected eight first-time call-ups for matches against Australia and India.

The Selecao subsequently recorded two victories and a draw, with several emerging players receiving their first opportunities at senior international level.

The forthcoming encounters against Japan and Singapore therefore represent another opportunity for Ancelotti to evaluate his options before moving towards greater continuity in selection.

Among the latest additions, Marlon Gomes could have one of the clearest opportunities to influence Ancelotti's plans, with the Shakhtar midfielder being assessed in a deeper role during preparations for the Japan fixture.

The 22-year-old, formerly of Vasco da Gama, has developed into a versatile central midfielder capable of contributing defensively and carrying possession into advanced areas.

According to Brazilian outlet Trivela, Gomes has averaged 4.5 tackles and completed 96% of his passes across four Champions League appearances this season.

His versatility could be particularly useful as Ancelotti considers different midfield combinations involving Arsenal's Bruno Guimaraes, Manchester United's Andrey Santos and Aston Villa's Joao Gomes.

Another intriguing inclusion is Manchester City youngster Allan, who received his first Brazil call-up despite playing just 10 minutes of Premier League football following his summer arrival from Palmeiras.

The 22-year-old has struggled for regular opportunities under Enzo Maresca, although his defensive commitment and ability to operate on either flank offer Ancelotti a different option in attack.

Allan recorded four goals and three assists in 21 Brazilian top-flight appearances for Palmeiras, according to the statistics highlighted by Trivela.

Jonathan Jesus, meanwhile, provides another possibility at centre-back, having established himself at Cruzeiro this season.

The 22-year-old is naturally right-footed but regularly operates on the left side of central defence, where Arsenal's Gabriel Magalhaes is among Ancelotti's established options.

Ancelotti previously praised Jonathan's physical strength, pace and intelligence, while his distribution could also prove valuable in Brazil's attempts to build from the back.

Corinthians midfielder Andre Luiz, 20, offers energy and the ability to arrive in attacking positions from deep, having contributed four goals and two assists in 24 league appearances.

Shakhtar winger Alisson Santana, 21, has also caught the eye with his direct running and one-on-one ability, averaging 4.3 successful dribbles per match in the Ukrainian league this season.

Whether all five newcomers receive playing time remains uncertain, particularly against a Japan side that will provide Brazil with a demanding test on Saturday.

Ancelotti has already indicated that he wants to experiment with Bournemouth forward Rayan in midfield, while Marlon Gomes has been considered for a defensive midfield role.

Those decisions could offer an early indication of which younger players are closest to earning a regular place when Brazil begin preparing more directly for the 2028 Copa America.

#1813. 'I have a letter from a nine-year-old fan on my cupboard door' - Sheffield United's Amy Andrews motivated by taking unconventional route

There is no lip service being paid, on whatever side of the barrier you stand. Amy Andrews was one of those girls who leant across in her youth, now it is she who makes a few memories for the smiling faces of the young Sheffield United fans that greet her at Bramall Lane.

“You don't realise who's there waiting for you, there could be a child that's been waiting for so long to meet you and for you to just sign something and have a photo with them and it means the world,” says the 26-year-old forward who is in her second year with the Blades in WSL2.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

“We have the opportunity to give back to our fans that spend money and time coming to watch us. We get letters from the fans. I had one from a nine-year-old that I've stuck on my cupboard door. I look at it every day and it motivates me.”

Her own story is an inspirational one. Andrews didn’t get into professional football via the now conventional route through an elite club academy.

She had to go to America to find her path after two club academies near her Birmingham home chewed her up and spat her out.

“I felt like we weren't really cared for,” laments Andrews. “It made me quit the game for a year and then I went back to my local club with my best friends because I just wanted to enjoy my football again.

“Then America came up and that's how I got here, I had to take the harder route, I've been fighting against opinions and a different background all my life.

“There's kids now that have got Nike deals who are assigned to WSL teams but haven't played in the WSL.

“Going to America (she attended Western Illinois) shaped me to be the player and person I am today, because you just learn so much, leaving home at 18. It was quite difficult at first but I got used to it in the end, and I'd do it again if I could and would definitely recommend it.”

When she returned home she had spells in the second tier with Durham Cestria and Newcastle United. But after falling out of favour at Newcastle when new investment came in, Sheffield United offered her a fresh start in July 2025.

“When I met with the coaching staff and analysts, they valued me a lot, they showed me clips of me playing and how they're going to bring that out of me,” says Andrews.

“I just thought I need to get a hard-working club that's going to play me and value me.”

She has found her home in Sheffield. Andrews scored 10 goals last season - “United helped me rediscover my confidence” - and bagged her first hat-trick against former club Durham at Bramall Lane in September.

“That’s something I’ve had on my list of goals since I've turned professional, so it meant a lot,” she beams. “But I immediately turned my thoughts to when can I get my next one.”

It may happen on Saturday night against Bristol City at Bramall Lane, a showcase game for which adult tickets are £10, concessions £5.

“The pitch at Bramall Lane is so smooth, like a carpet,” she says.

“It's a privilege to play there. I remember playing for Newcastle at St James’ Park against AC Milan, scoring the equaliser in the last minute and then a penalty in the penalty shoot-out; that was unbelievable. I played there when there were 38,000 fans - amazing

“It gave me a taster of what I want to achieve. I know I'm good enough to get to the WSL. There's no point playing football if you don't have those goals, because what are you fighting for?

“I never got that opportunity to take the conventional route when I was growing up, so that's what I'm striving for. That's what motivates me.

“I feel like the odd one out. I'm so hungry to prove people wrong. I want people to hear my story.

Zlatan Ibrahimovic has shed light on just how much AC Milan mean to him, labelling it the ‘most important’ club he has represented.

Today marks the launch of ‘Il Milan nel Mondo’, Mauro Suma’s new book exploring the Rossoneri’s reach beyond both Milan and Italy. Several Rossoneri Legends will join the author at the launch this morning, including Daniele Massaro, Demetrio Albertini and Filippo Galli.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Ibrahimovic wrote a foreword in the book, which has been relayed by MilanNews. The RedBird Capital senior advisor spoke about just how much the club means to him, after his two spells as a player and now his time as an executive.

“Milan are the most important team in my life. And it’s also the only one that convinced me to return. In my career, I’ve worn legendary shirts, played in wonderful cities, and won everywhere. But Milan was something different,” he said.

“It was the only club that truly drew me back, the only one where I felt the need to start over. Convincing Zlatan to return isn’t easy. It’s not easy for anyone. Yet, with Milan, it’s happened more than once.

“This means that between me and these colours, a bond has been created that goes beyond football, beyond trophies, even beyond time. Victory remains in the halls of fame; some teams, however, stay with you. AC Milan belongs to this category.

“The first time, AC Milan brought me happiness, the second, love. In the Rossoneri, I found a sense of belonging that is increasingly rare in modern football. Because starting an adventure with a club can happen. Returning a second time, and then again, means that the club and its fans have become part of you.

“AC Milan are the most successful Italian club at international level, but it’s not just a collection of trophies. It’s an identity. It’s a way of being in football and in the world. Wherever it goes, it leaves a mark. And those who join AC Milan, sometimes, never leave.”

Ibrahimovic signed the first time in August 2010 after an experience at Barcelona that wasn’t a positive one, and he helped Milan to the Scudetto with a 14-goal haul. He won the Capocannoniere the next season, doubling that tally.

He returned in 2019 and scored 25 goals in 37 appearances in his first two campaigns, securing a return to European competitions. At the end of his third season, the climb was complete: the Rossoneri won their 19th league title.

Then, in June 2023 came his emotional farewell at San Siro, before Zlatan returned to the club but wearing a suit and tie.

#1811. Harry Kane receives new England GOAT verdict as 120-goal prediction made (exclusive)

By Ben Knapton | 13 Nov 2026 16:30

Harry Kane has usurped Wayne Rooney as the best England player of his generation, but he still trails the 1966 World Cup winners among the all-time greats, Darren Bent has exclusively told Sports Mole.

Kane now stands alone in both appearances and goals for the England men's national team, having broken Peter Shilton's record of 125 caps with his 126th senior international outing against Croatia on Thursday night.

The Bayern Munich talisman had already held the England all-time goals record for over three years, surpassing Wayne Rooney's 53 in March 2023, and his penalty in the Nations League took him onto 92 for the men's team.

Kane also reached the zenith of individual footballing achievements by winning the Ballon d'Or last month, but the England captain is yet to lead his nation to a World Cup or Euros triumph.

As a result, ex-England, Aston Villa and Tottenham Hotspur striker Bent - who scored four goals in 13 England games - believes that Kane is still not quite in the conversation with Sir Bobby Moore and Sir Bobby Charlton.

"It's really difficult to go against those boys from the 60s. They climbed the mountain and won the World Cup, and there will obviously have been Ballon d'Or winners in that team as well," Bent told Sports Mole via MrQ sportsbook.

"It's difficult to automatically put Harry Kane above them. But certainly in my generation, it would either be him or Wayne Rooney as the greatest England player.

"When you look at Kane being the all-time record caps holder and the all-time record goalscorer, it's hard to put Rooney above him. I'd probably say that, for this modern generation, it would be Kane.

"If Kane were to win the World Cup, he would automatically go into a bracket alongside the likes of Bobby Charlton as one of England's greatest players. But he's already in the conversation, and that's massive in itself. To put him in the conversation with those greats, legends and icons is special."

With an unrivalled 92 goals in an unparalleled 126 caps, Kane finds the net at a rate of 0.73 goals per game for the England national team, compared to Rooney's 0.44 and Charlton's 0.46.

The Tottenham legend turns 34 next year, but barring injury or an unexpected early retirement, Euro 2028 and the 2030 World Cup are very much on the horizon.

Asking AI to predict how many England goals Kane could rack up before retirement, the 33-year-old is projected to find the net 120 times for his country, should he call it quits after the 2030 World Cup.

Such a total would currently put Kane third on the all-time international scorers list, above Ali Daei (108) and only behind Lionel Messi (126) and Cristiano Ronaldo (146).

Kane is already joint-sixth in the charts alongside Robert Lewandowski, and two more will take him level with Romelu Lukaku's 94 for Belgium, while he needs three to match Sunil Chhetri's 95 for India.

Darren Bent was speaking to Sports Mole on behalf of MrQ Live Casino.

#1807. VAR a scourge on the Premier League as Forest denied by off-field meddling

Almost £3.5bn was splurged on transfers this summer in a league supposedly described as the best in the world, so why does VAR continue to prove so ineffective and divisive?

Seven years after its introduction, it remains a scourge on the Premier League and here at the City Ground was another exhibit of maddening off-field meddling.

Tottenham Hotspur avoided a third successive defeat after the crucial intervention of VAR prevented Neco Williams from securing Oliver Glasner his first win as Nottingham Forest’s head coach.

The big moment occurred in the 65th minute. Morgan Gibbs-White’s chip over Antonin Kinsky should have been dealt with by Sandro Tonali and Jan Paul van Hecke but both players got themselves in a muddle and Williams bundled the ball in from almost on the goal-line.

Replays appeared to show the ball went in off Williams’ knee and he was protecting his face with his hands to avoid a stray boot. The VAR review ruled that Williams had handled the ball, yet in this billion-pound industry there was not one camera angle which proved entirely conclusive.

On this occasion the VAR official was Peter Bankes, recommending to referee Craig Pawson that the goal be disallowed. Williams said: “It’s a goal. VAR is there when there is a clear and obvious error and for me that is not clear and obvious. I’ve seen the images and the replays and at not one moment did I think I handballed it because I never did. I headed it in between my arms. I’m at a loss at that one, it’s disappointing. If you’re going to pause it, it’s going to look like it hit my arm but it didn’t hit my arm.”

Glasner and the other Forest players were also incensed, and once again supporters are questioning how critical moments in matches are being decided by officials sitting at Stockley Park. “I think the VAR can’t intervene when he is guessing,” said Glasner. “I told the referee after the game that I felt the goal should have stood.

“The VAR should say to stay with the onfield decision because it is about strengthening the referee. If it’s not 100 per cent clear, stick to the onfield decision.  We had a briefing before the season that the threshold for VAR intervention this year should be very high which is why this is wrong.”

While Tottenham were perhaps fortunate to pick up their first point, they are still waiting to score their first Premier League goal of the season. They did not manage a shot on target.

The grand £350m rebuild is proving a slow-burner and it is only Mykhailo Mudryk who will have cause to remember such a dull affair. Signed on loan from Chelsea on deadline day, Mudryk made his first appearance since November 2024 after being suspended by the Football Association following a positive test for performance-enhancing meldonium.

One of their summer arrivals, Omar Marmoush, wasted their best chance in the 16th minute by drilling a shot wide of the post. De Zerbi said: “In the last third we have to improve. We have to maybe keep more calm when we are very close to doing something important.

“If we improve in the last third I think we can score many goals because we have the players with big qualities. We could have scored three or four goals.

Considering we were only all working together on Thursday for the first time, this is the right spirit and the right way to move on.” On Mudryk, De Zerbi said: “He’s working to reach the best physical condition and he needs time.”
