The big headline news from Tottenham is that Mykhailo Mudryk is on the bench.

Signed from Chelsea on deadline day on an initial loan, Mudryk was once branded as a future Ballon d’Or winner by Roberto De Zerbi after they worked together at Shakhtar.

Mudryk has not played a competitive match since November 2024 after being suspended by the Football Association following a positive test for performance-enhancing meldonium.

Enzo Fernández’s record deal to Manchester City was facilitated by English-founded agency Unique Sports Management, it can be revealed.

Fernández sealed a £125m move from Chelsea on deadline day, equalling the UK transfer record of Alexander Isak to Liverpool a year ago.

Football Association documents due to be published later in the season will show Unique to have played their part in the biggest transfer of the summer.

Fernández is represented by The Elegant Game, headed by ex-Argentina international Javier Pastore, although he is not registered with the FA for transfers in England.

Unique, which also represented Anthony Gordon for his move to Barcelona, were brought in to close the deal, which was agreed between clubs on deadline day afternoon.

The English-founded agency have Marc Guéhi, who moved to City in January, on their books and their summer deals included Gordon to Barca, Maxence Lacroix to Chelsea and Taylor Harwood-Bellis to Aston Villa. Troy Parrott, who scored the winner for Real Betis against Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid, is also in the Unique stable.

Will this be third time lucky for Tottenham Hotspur after their £300m+ summer reset?

In typical Tottenham fashion, their start to the Premier League season has not been straightforward with two defeats, five goals conceded and none scored so far.

The popular opinion is that it will eventually click, but Tottenham’s supporters are still scarred by those two successive 17th-placed finishes.

Forest have won their last four games against Spurs, so it will be an early sign of promise if Roberto De Zerbi can secure a positive result here.

Enzo Maresca believes streetwise Enzo Fernández will give Manchester City an extra winning edge – as he told his record £125 million signing to forget about the size of the fee.

City made the Argentina midfielder the joint most expensive purchase in Premier League history with their deadline day swoop from Chelsea.

Maresca has opted against naming Fernández among his captains’ leadership group, which features Ruben Dias, Erling Haaland, Marc Guéhi and Gianluigi Donnarumma.

But the Italian – who knows Fernández well from their time together at Stamford Bridge – is confident his fierce competitive instincts will bring an added dimension to his side.

“I don’t know if it’s streetwise but he knows how to win,” Maresca said, who is in line to hand Fernández his debut against Coventry on Saturday. “When you want to compete or win, it’s much more important to have players that already know how to do that than players who have never done it in the past.

“Enzo is not the only one. This squad has many players who know how to win titles and how to compete and this is what we are looking for.

“I know Enzo quite well and I know what he can bring to the team. He is a winner, [has] a winner’s mentality and knows how to win [after] the World Cup, Club World Cup [success].

“I just said he is a winner and when you belong to the squad and another winning player arrives, they are always happy.

“I can promise you that in the last four or five days, four or five players from the squad were asking if was coming or not because they wanted him to be with us. It’s very important that he is with us.”

Maresca said he planned to use Fernandez predominantly as a No 6 or No 8 depending on the game. “I see Enzo as a six, a little bit more deep, or [an eight] a little higher arriving in the box,” he said.

Good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of the Saturday afternoon 3pm kick-offs of which we are treated to a rare number this week as Sky and TNT Sports decide to inconvenience only 10 sets of matchgoing supporters rather than the usual 12 or 14. The matches start, purely alphabetically, with unbeaten Brentford hosting Sunderland, Leeds United travelling to Brighton and Hove Albion’s Amex Stadium where they have never won and have come away with only three points in their seven visits, the something’s-got-to-give quasi derby between winless Fulham and pointless Palace, leaders Man City hosting Coventry City for the Sky Blue Cup and Tottenham head to Nottingham Forest in pursuit of their first point to spoil the gaiety of a nation.

We have Mike McGrath reporting from the Etihad and John Percy at the City Ground and I will endeavour to keep you up to date with developments at the other three grounds via various methods. Forest vs Spurs seems the most consequential of the fixtures, not because either manager is in any danger but because now the window has closed it should give us a clearer picture of how Roberto De Zerbi plans to marshal his surfeit of wingers into a coherent attack that can break their goalscoring duck and how he proposes to organise a back four that have shipped five goals.

Fulham and Palace have come in for a lot of criticism regarding their recruitment and while I can understand the frustration of the former’s fans for doing so much business with Real Madrid, I think Gonzalo García is a proper player and will shine over the course of the season.

Palace, I think, are paying the price for the January splurge on Brennan Johnson and Jorgen Strand Larsen, not just the inflated fees but the sizeable wages on players who contributed almost nothing. I was at Leeds vs Brentford last week and there was plenty to admire about both sides but fear for Leeds’ so-far commendable resilience at their Amex knacker’s yard and wonder whether Sunderland will be able to live with Brentford’s pace. Manchester City vs Coventry, meanwhile, probably will not give us the Bouaddi-Fernández-Anderson £325m midfield from the start but we might be given a glimpse.

#1806. CorSport: Doing everything but scoring – Ramos and Amorim pursue missing goals

Goncalo Ramos is doing just about everything that can be asked of a centre-forward, except scoring goals regularly.

This morning’s Corriere dello Sport (via MilanNews) has a section headlined: ‘Now all Gonçalo needs is goals’. The Portuguese striker – who arrived at Milan in the summer for over €70m from PSG – has scored only three times so far in the league and Europa League.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Despite this, his involvement is constant and his stats speak for themselves. Ramos ranks second among strikers in Serie A in receptions, touches, and duels won, while he’s third in passes made. He ranks first in both interceptions and balls recovered, showing the spirit of sacrifice.

Expanding the discussion to forwards (so wingers included), Ramos is second in the league when it comes to total number of fouls committed and drawn with 41 in total, bettered only by Nicolo Cambiaghi of Bologna with 47.

Now, however, Ruben Amorim and the fans are expecting a breakthrough in scoring goals, which is what he was signed for and what is needed with a price tag so high. Only two have come from open play, and one of these was a gift from RB Salzburg.

A new striker will arrive in January who will have to alternate with the Portuguese. Fatigue could be one reason for Ramos being flat in front of goal given he has almost always started, as Francesco Camarda does not seem to have Amorim’s full faith yet.

#1804. Mauricio Pochettino's record against every Premier League club after Man United appointment

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 13 Nov 2026 17:28

Manchester United have appointed Mauricio Pochettino as their new head coach, with the Argentine replacing Michael Carrick, who was sacked on Thursday after the club’s worst-ever start to a Premier League season left them in the relegation zone.

The 54-year-old, who led the United States to the 2026 World Cup, where they topped Group D before a 4-1 last-16 defeat to Belgium, has now signed for the Red Devils on a deal that runs until the summer of 2029.

With Old Trafford the seventh senior post of a managerial career that began at Espanyol in January 2009, Pochettino returns to club football for the first time since leaving Chelsea by mutual consent in May 2024.

Having also managed Southampton and Tottenham Hotspur, Pochettino arrives at Old Trafford with a wealth of Premier League experience ahead of his first game in charge, a daunting trip to Liverpool on Sunday, November 22.

With that in mind, Sports Mole takes a look at Pochettino’s record against every club in the current Premier League, as well as the sides he is yet to come up against.

Pochettino’s Premier League record against Arsenal reads three wins, eight draws and four defeats from 15 games, a middling return given how rarely north London derbies are kind to anyone.

All three of those top-flight victories came with Spurs, while his last top-flight meeting with the Gunners ended in a 5-0 thrashing as Chelsea boss in April 2024.

Pochettino has a solid Premier League record against Aston Villa, winning four, drawing two and losing three of his nine meetings with them in the competition.

Three of those top-flight triumphs came with Tottenham, including a 3-1 victory on the opening weekend of 2019-20, but he failed to beat Villa in two Premier League attempts with Chelsea.

Bournemouth have been among Pochettino’s favourite Premier League opponents, with seven wins, two draws and just one defeat in 10 top-flight meetings.

The Argentine’s sides have so far scored 24 Premier League goals against the Cherries and conceded only four, including a 5-1 away win in 2015 and a 5-0 Boxing Day rout in 2018.

Brentford are the only current Premier League side Pochettino has faced in the competition and never beaten.

Both Premier League meetings came during his season at Chelsea, with the Bees winning 2-0 in October 2023 before the sides drew 2-2 in March 2024.

Pochettino boasts an impressive Premier League record against Brighton, winning five of his seven top-flight meetings with the Seagulls, including both with Chelsea.

The 54-year-old’s only Premier League defeat to Brighton came in a 3-0 loss in October 2019, just weeks before his Tottenham exit.

Pochettino faced Chelsea 13 times in the Premier League before managing them, winning five, drawing two and losing six.

The standout league result was Tottenham’s 5-3 victory on New Year’s Day 2015, while the infamous 2-2 Premier League draw at Stamford Bridge in May 2016 ended Spurs’ title hopes.

No club in this season’s Premier League has lost to Pochettino more often in the competition than Crystal Palace, who have managed one draw and one win in 15 top-flight meetings with him.

The Argentine’s sides have beaten Palace in 11 successive top-flight games, and his 2.67 Premier League points per game against them is his best against any club he has faced more than six times in the competition.

Everton have been kind Premier League opponents for Pochettino, who has won eight, drawn six and lost just two of his 16 top-flight meetings with them.

Pochettino’s teams have scored 33 Premier League goals against the Toffees, including a 6-2 win at Goodison Park in December 2018 and a 6-0 home thrashing with Chelsea in April 2024.

Pochettino has a perfect Premier League record against Fulham, winning all six top-flight meetings across his spells at Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea.

The Argentine’s teams have scored 13 Premier League goals against the Cottagers and conceded just two, with Fulham yet to take a single top-flight point off him.

Hull City have had no answer to Pochettino either, losing all six of their Premier League meetings with him.

Pochettino’s teams have scored 19 top-flight goals and conceded three against the Tigers, highlighted by a 7-1 win at the KCOM Stadium on the final day of the 2016-17 Premier League season.

Pochettino has never faced Leeds United in the Premier League, with his only meeting with them coming in the FA Cup fifth round in February 2024.

Conor Gallagher’s 90th-minute winner gave his Chelsea side a 3-2 FA Cup win at Stamford Bridge, meaning Pochettino is yet to lose to the Whites in any competition.

Liverpool have been Pochettino’s toughest Premier League opponents, with just three wins, five draws and eight defeats in 16 top-flight meetings.

Pochettino’s 0.88 Premier League points per game against them is his worst against any club he has faced more than twice in the competition, and outside the league he also lost the 2019 Champions League final and the 2024 League Cup showpiece to the Reds.

Pochettino has won four, drawn five and lost seven of his 16 Premier League games against Manchester City.

Tottenham beat City in three successive top-flight meetings between September 2015 and October 2016, while his Chelsea side twice held Pep Guardiola’s side in the league, including a 4-4 thriller in November 2023.

Pochettino’s new employers have had the better of him in the Premier League, with five wins, three draws and seven defeats in 15 top-flight meetings.

The 54-year-old’s best league results against the Red Devils include a 3-0 win at Old Trafford in August 2018 and a 4-3 Chelsea victory in April 2024, though United also beat his Spurs side in the 2018 FA Cup semi-final.

Pochettino’s Premier League record against Newcastle is otherwise evenly balanced, with seven wins, one draw and six defeats in 14 games, and 23 goals both scored and conceded.

The Argentine’s Southampton side won 4-0 in a league clash in March 2014, but Tottenham crashed to a 5-1 loss at St James’ Park on the final day of the 2015-16 Premier League season.

Pochettino has faced Nottingham Forest twice in the Premier League, both times as Chelsea boss, winning one and losing one.

Anthony Elanga’s goal earned the Tricky Trees a 1-0 league win at Stamford Bridge in September 2023, before the Blues won 3-2 at the City Ground in the Premier League in May 2024.

Sunderland are one of three current Premier League clubs Pochettino is unbeaten against in the competition, with four wins and five draws in nine top-flight meetings.

The pick of those Premier League results was a 4-1 home win with Spurs in January 2016, although he has lost twice to the Black Cats in cup competitions.

Pochettino lost all three of his Premier League meetings with Tottenham as Southampton boss, two of them by 3-2 scorelines.

The Argentine manager then won both English top-flight  games against his old club with Chelsea in 2023-24, including a 4-1 victory in north London in November 2023.

Coventry City and Ipswich Town are the only current Premier League clubs Pochettino has never faced in any competition.

The Sky Blues ended a 25-year absence from the top flight this season, which means they were outside the Premier League throughout his spells at Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea.

The Argentine’s first meeting with Coventry should come when they visit Old Trafford on Saturday, December 5, in what is scheduled to be his fourth league game in charge.

Ipswich’s only recent top-flight season came after he had left English football, and with United having already hosted them on August 30, his first meeting with the Tractor Boys is set for Portman Road on Saturday, April 17, 2027.

#1803. ‘Won’t be far off’ - Ex-Aston Villa and Wolves boss Paul Lambert issues optimistic Leeds United verdict

Former Aston Villa and Wolverhampton Wanderers manager Paul Lambert does not believe Leeds United will be far from European football this season.

The club sit ninth in the Premier League table after 10 games and promising displays have sparked hope of a push for Europe.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Whites boss Daniel Farke has taken care to manage expectations, but there are plenty of pundits holding the belief that qualification is a possibility.

Among them is Lambert, who has claimed the club’s home form could prove key.

He told BetVictor: “Leeds United are another fabulous club with a great fanbase. They started really well. You'll get a couple of dodgy results here and there in the Premier League. Is Europe a possibility?

“Leeds won't be far off. Their home form at Elland Road with that crowd is key. Even away from home, Leeds look like a proper team with good togetherness and spirit.

“I think they've done really well and I think the manager's done great.”

The international break has presented Leeds with some respite, although many of their key figures are currently away on international duty.

Farke’s men were last in action last weekend, defeating Tottenham Hotspur 1-0 at Elland Road courtesy of a Noah Okafor goal.

Leeds’ manager said: “There's no replacement for this winning feeling after such a game in the dressing room. It's great to have this winning feeling back.

“All the credit and all my compliments go to the boys' terrific performance against a really in-form Tottenham side.

“It was important today to show this unity and commitment. We were technically spot on in order to avoid all their processes and all their individual quality in order to score goals and reduce them to very, very little already in the first half.”

#1802. CM: Three names on the list as Milan begin difficult hunt for Modric’s heir

AC Milan must start thinking about the midfield of the future, and there are reportedly a few names on the list of ideas.

At 41 years of age Luka Modric, still remains simply irreplaceable for Ruben Amorim and for Milan. However, given that his deal expires at the end of the season, the Rossoneri management have a duty to also look to the future and prepare for the post-Modric era.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The scouting team are very active in England, Spain, Belgium, and France, looking for the right players for Amorim’s footballing philosophy. Among the priorities for next season is identifying the right player to potentially take the reins as a deeper-lying playmaker.

Calciomercato.com report that three players have attracted considerable interest from Milan. One of them is Bournemouth’s Alex Scott, but he remains a dream at the moment because Arsenal and Chelsea have already swooped in on him.

The 23-year-old was called up to the England squad for the last break because manager Thomas Tuchel is very keen on him, but there’s a significant obstacle: the price tag. In England, there is even talk of a €100m+ asking price, given the clubs interested.

The spotlight has recently turned on Brighton’s Yasin Ayari too. He’s a highly versatile midfielder, performing at a high level both as a defensive midfielder and behind the striker. The Swede’s deal runs out in 2027 making him a big opportunity, but Brighton have a one-year option to.

Finally, we arrive at the new name on the list: Adem Zorgane of Union-Saint Gilloise. Scouts like what they have seen from the Algerian, who combines physicality with good technical ability. He would likely be the cheapest of the three, but his potential is high in the eyes of Milan.

#1801. Spurs transfer news: Mikey Moore loan plan being 'considered' by club chiefs

By Darren Plant | 13 Nov 2026 17:30

Tottenham Hotspur are reportedly giving consideration to terminating Mikey Moore's loan stint at FC Koln.

With the academy graduate not viewed as a regular starter by Roberto De Zerbi, the decision was made for the 19-year-old to move elsewhere during the summer transfer window.

On the back of earning game time with Rangers in 2025-26, Moore was allowed to move to the Bundesliga.

However, despite making nine appearances for the German side, it could be argued that the winger is not producing his best form.

According to TEAMtalk, that may lead to Moore returning to North London at the midway point of the campaign.

The report alleges that both clubs are open to ending Moore's time in Germany in January.

FC Koln are said to have no interest in signing the England Under-20 international on a permanent basis.

Moore has failed to contributed a goal or assist in six starts and three substitute outings in all competitions.

If Spurs choose to terminate Moore's time at FC Koln, he would be forced to remain in North London for the rest of the season.

That is a consequence of FIFA rules dictating that a player can only play for two different clubs in the same season, unless seasons in different countries overlap.

Moore played three times for Spurs before signing for FC Koln, subsequently reducing his options moving forward.

This scenario increases the changes of Moore staying at FC Koln for the entire season.

Bohemians boss Alan Reynolds added: “Clarke is a talented attacking midfielder, left-footed, with an eye for a pass. He’s a creative type, with really good box to box energy, and can play in any of the front three areas in midfield, out wide or the number 10.

#1794. Mauricio Pochettino will ditch four Man Utd stars – the winners and losers under new boss

Mauricio Pochettino is poised to take the reins at Manchester United in the club’s latest attempt to reset the clock.

Having been regarded as a genuine candidate for the job at Old Trafford on three occasions in the past, the Argentine now gets his chance in Manchester where United’s situation is more dire than ever.

With Michael Carrick’s exit confirmed, Pochettino will inherit a squad that has been routinely booed off the pitch by a fanbase thoroughly disenchanted with a lack of effort on it. While there may be hopes of recruitment in the January transfer window, Pochettino will have to work with what he has at his disposal until then.

Metro looks across the United squad to identify whose prospects look brighter than ever with the new manager en route – and those who face the axe.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

With Benjamin Sesko starting just two matches this season before injury struck again, Bryan Mbeumo has spent most of the campaign operating up top. He could remain in that role until Sesko is fit again but both he and Matheus Cunha stand to benefit in their natural positions under the new regime.

Pochettino has favoured inverted wingers to help create overloads in the middle with Cunha in particular tailor made for that role.

Moussa Dembele evolved into one of the Premier League’s most dominant midfielders at Tottenham under Pochettino, carrying on the work started by Martin Jol at Fulham with the Belgian. Kobbie Mainoo lacks Dembele’s outstanding athleticism but his press resistance and running power with the ball will be regarded as key assets for Pochettino.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Mainoo does not have the constant high-energy output Pochettino has traditionally demanded of his midfielders but he has improved his engine over the last two years and his ability to break the lines could also see him play a key role.

Erik ten Hag, Ruben Amorim and Michael Carrick all lauded the qualities of Mason Mount despite injuries ensuring they never saw the best of him. Pochettino could be another to look favourably upon him if he can prove his fitness.

When in negotiations with Chelsea back in 2023, Pochettino was eager for the club to end a contract stand-off with the midfielder and was desperate to keep him and make him a key component of his rebuild west London. His own arrival came too late to revive negotiations however with Mount joining United that summer.

Mount’s work rate has never been in doubt and his abilities to run off the ball or intelligently drop into space could be vital. But with just one start in the Premier League this season, the same old doubts are in place.

In October, former United captain Gary Neville called time on the Mainoo-Youri Tielemans partnership, neither dynamic or athletic enough to last the course in the Premier League. There may only be one winner with the Belgian perhaps most at risk.

Tielemans is adept in keeping possession and progressing play but his lack of drive up the pitch is seemingly at odds with how Pochettino likes to set up his midfield. Pochettino was also said to have turned down the chance to sign the midfielder on at least one occasion after his name was put forward by the Tottenham board.

The same concerns for Tielemans could also apply for another summer recruit in Andrey Santos who looks to be another passive operator based on evidence to date.

The emphasis Pochettino puts on his full-backs has been huge during his time in the Premier League but it is the area of the pitch where United are perhaps at their weakest. Diogo Dalot’s shortcomings on the right continue to be exposed while a long-term replacement for Luke Shaw is well overdue.

Dalot’s prospects are brighter – while his final ball is consistently short of the required standard, his ability to get up and down the pitch will be important. Shaw can no longer offer that kind of service on the left and Pochettino may favour the energy of Patrick Dorgu.

Pochettino helped nurture Shaw at Southampton before his £27million move to Manchester in 2014 but the 31-year-old will now struggle to provide the intensity the role demands.

United’s defence has been an utter mess and with the exception of perhaps Leny Yoro, all should consider their futures uncertain. But at 34, Maguire is perhaps the most at risk.

Pochettino favours a high defensive line, requiring centre-halves with pace to live with it. Maguire will turn 34 in March and has been at the heart of a backline that has conceded 19 goals in 10 Premier League games this season.

Pochettino may favour the younger legs of Yoro and Ayden Heaven while Lisandro Martinez’s ability to build from the back could keep him in the picture for now.

#1793. Hull City an inspiration for decades to come as Sheffield United and co take on Championship's parachute regiment

Along with Ipswich Town and Coventry City, if Hull can stay in the Premier League next season, it will be a shot in the arm for the Championship, just as Leeds United and even more so Sunderland's 2025-26s were.

Because at times in recent years the gap between the top two divisions has felt almost unbridgeable.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Since the introduction of parachute payments in 2006-07, 29 of the 60 relegated teams were promoted back to the Premier League whilst being eligible for them, making them less parachutes, more bungee ropes.

Nevertheless, Coventry and Hull got up last season without them, Hull on the back of a 2024-25 where they only escaped relegation on goal difference, then rebuilt their squad under transfer restrictions which prevented them buying players or even paying loan fees in either window.

As Wilder's Blades try to scramble back this season after a summer of big cutbacks when they lost their parachute payment, it is something to take cheer from.

The veteran manager called the Tigers: "An unbelievable example for the next ten, 15, 20 years in the Championship is Hull City.

"They find themselves in the Premier League which in a way I love because it doesn't go on stats at all, it goes on character, togetherness, spirit.

"It goes on ability and a group that had young players as well as the senior players, and we know quite a lot of them because they played at this club (or Middlesbrough under Wilder) and it just shows you money doesn't buy everything.

"It's about constructing a team that can go nine months and find a way to win. They found a way to win all season, in the (play-off) semi-final and the final.

"They're in the Premier League and they won't give a damn about anyone's opinion about them. Good luck to them."

And despite signing 18 players in the summer, Hull have given themselves a good chance of staying up with a strong start to the campaign built around the core who defeated Boro at Wembley in the play-off final, rather than the shiny new additions presumably intended by the recruitment department to replace them.

Meanwhile, the three teams level on points at the top of the Championship in November's international break – Birmingham City, Boro and Stoke City – have mounted their challenges without parachute money. So too Swansea City and Queens Park Rangers in the play-off places and the Blades two points back.

"Knowing Middlesbrough, the owner (Steve Gibson)'s been incredibly supportive of that football club for a long time," reflected Wilder. "They buy, they sell, they've invested the money from Hayden Hackney and Morgan Rogers.

"There's all different ways but they've been ambitious in their approach.

"Coventry sold well – (Viktor) Gjokeres, Gus (Hamer) and other players.

"It (having a parachute) isn't a guarantee.

"Stoke City have got good owners, a great manager and I'm sure Mark (Robins) will crack it this season. They've not been in the top ten since they've come out of the Premier League (in 2018) and it was a club that under Tony Pulis were top eight for a number of years, accumulating funds.

"It's not always a gimme. That's how difficult the Championship is."

‘He looks like an immovable object in that team. That’s what it feels like because he’s just slid in there and taken that place. He looks dominant, aggressive and accustomed to wearing the Arsenal shirt.

‘He looks like he belongs there. But let’s not forget about Saliba and what he was doing when he was in the team. It’s a problem but it’s a problem that I hope Mikel Arteta will enjoy because he’s got two top centre-backs vying to be in the team.

‘It’s a good position to be in. I think we will see Konsa sometimes playing right-back.’

Arsenal’s nearest challengers going into the November international break is Brighton, who have won seven of their ten league games to climb to second in the Premier League.

‘Brighton could be Arsenal’s main challenge to the title this season,’ Shearer added.

‘I think Liverpool are in transition. Chelsea, same thing. They still have plenty of work to do with those football clubs.

‘Brighton have been incredible. The football that they’re playing, I mean, in Europe too, whether that will hinder them the longer the season goes on I don’t know, but they’re managing really well at the minute.

‘I don’t think they’re going to go away. I think there’ll be around for the majority of the season.’

Arsenal’s first game back following the international break is a potentially tricky trip to St James’ Park to face Newcastle United.

Alan Shearer believes that Brighton will prove to be Arsenal’s main title challengers over the likes of Manchester City this season.

Defending champions Arsenal are now five points clear at the top of the league table following their hard-fought 1-0 win at home to Hull City on Saturday.

Conversely, it was another bad weekend for Manchester City as their third successive league defeat saw Enzo Maresca’s side slip to third.

That defeat for City means Brighton are now second in the table after Fabian Hurzeler’s side continued their superb start to the season with a 2-0 win over Brentford.

The Seagulls have already beaten both Arsenal and City in the league this season, with no team scoring more goals and only Arsenal conceding fewer after ten games.

And former title winner Shearer believes that their early-season performances are evidence enough that they will provide the sternest test to Mikel Arteta’s side in this season’s title race.

‘Brighton could be Arsenal’s main challenge to the title this season,’ Shearer told Betfair.

‘I think Liverpool are in transition. Chelsea, same thing. They still have plenty of work to do with those football clubs.

‘Brighton have been incredible. The football that they’re playing, I mean, in Europe too, whether that will hinder them the longer the season goes on I don’t know, but they’re managing really well at the minute.

#1787. Harrogate Town 4 Altrincham 0: Hosts make use of numerical advantage after Leeds United youngster sent off

Harrogate Town returned to winning ways as they secured an emphatic 4-0 victory over Altrincham in the National League.

Simon Weaver’s men had failed to win any of their previous three games across all competitions, but were thoroughly deserving of three points at the Marcy Fitness Stadium.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Altrincham lost on-loan Leeds United prospect Reuben Lopata-White to a red card after just 13 minutes and the numerical disadvantage helped Harrogate spend the bulk of the afternoon in the driving seat.

Will McGowan opened the scoring early in the second half and the lead was doubled by Morgan Williams just 10 minutes later. Michael Craig weighed in late on, smashing home a thunderous effort, before Rohan Vaughan weighed in to cap an excellent afternoon for the North Yorkshire outfit.

There was little to warm the cockles early on, as both sides took time defrosting on a crisp and biting November afternoon. Each enjoyed spells of posession but little was done with it and wing-backs remained tethered in their own halfs.

Harrogate frontman Shawn McCoulsky prompted the first ripple of applause by getting on the wrong side of Altrincham defender Jake Cooper. While he could not test Harry Isted between the Robins sticks, he did manage to win a corner.

Lewis Cass was left in a heap on the ground in the aftermath of the resulting delivery, but calls for a penalty fell on deaf ears.

The referee did react when Lopata-White - a young defender on loan at Altrincham from Leeds - lunged recklessly at Ellis Taylor. There was barely any hesitation from the official, who was quick to produce a red card.

Altrincham retreated deeper after going a man down and Harrogate seized the initiative, taking control of the affair. Clear-cut chances were initially at a premium but Lewis Cass came within a whisker of getting a boot on the end of an inviting Taylor cross from the left.

Little was being created for McCoulsky, although the forward did direct a header towards goal after rising to meet a Williams free-kick. Unfortunately for the hosts, it lacked power and was held with ease by Isted.

Taylor was proving increasingly problematic for the visitors, who struggled to stem the flow of attacks down the left flank as the first half progressed. He cut in side from the wing and forced Isted down to his right-hand side with a low drive to the near post.

Barely a minute later he reverted to being a provider and picked out Josh Hmami with a clever pass. The playmaker sent a low shot towards goal and saw it deflected just before it could test Isted.

Harrogate continued applying pressure into the dying embers of the first half and their final chance fell to Grant Horton, who met a delivery hung up at the back post but could only head into the side-netting.

A slick corner routine straight from the training ground opened Altrincham up within minutes of the restart but as stars aligned for McGowan, he lost his footing.

Craig had more luck when he pulled the trigger from distance, stinging the palms of Isted with a well-struck effort. Archie Baptistie followed suit with a long-range effort of his own, yet Isted was also equal to that.

Altrincham’s resolve was eventually cracked by McGowan, who swept home a left-footed shot after Taylor picked him out from the left.

Harrogate’s opener did not appear to have whet their appetite for goals, as the Sulphurites remained in the ascendency. McGowan jinked into space inside the box after being fed by Hmami, but was leaning back as he curled towards the top corner and found the wrong side of the crossbar.

Taylor, meanwhile, was evidently enjoying himself down the left-hand side. The former England youth international danced his way in from the left and saw a thunderous effort flash just over.

Altrincham had been offering little sign of life, yet Lucas Weaver had hearts in mouths when he drew an excellent save from Luke Hutchinson on the counter-attack. However, it was not to be the beginning of a Robins revival.

Williams sent a rasping shot in from distance and Isted was rendered helpless as it flew beyond him, doubling the home lead.

The frequency of attacks slowed somewhat in the closing stages of the first half but Harrogate’s grip on the game never loosened.

Altrincham simply could not move from first gear and eventually conceded a third when Craig hammered home the final goal of the afternoon.

Goal number four arrived in stoppage time, when substitute Vaughan rifled home a shot Isted was never going to get near.

#1786. Sebastian Pocognoli targets Tottenham star for Scotland allegiance switch from England

By Ben Sully | 13 Nov 2026 17:36, Last updated: 13 Nov 2026 17:38

Scotland Sebastien Pocognoli has admitted Tottenham Hotspur star Archie Gray is one of two Premier League players he is targeting for a potential allegiance switch from England.

Gray is currently with the England Under-21 squad after working his way through the national team age groups.

Barring any injury issues, the 20-year-old is likely to be part of Lee Carsley's squad for the Under-21 European Championships next summer.

However, progression to the England senior side is far from a foregone conclusion, partly because he is also eligible to represent Scotland.

Gray's father, Andy, represented Scotland at senior level, as did his grandfather, Frank, and his great-uncle, Eddie.

Pocognoli has admitted Gray and Everton's Hayden Hackney are his radar for potential allegiance switches to Scotland, who have not been put off by failing to convince Harvey Barnes to represent the Tartan Army under Steve Clarke.

“With Barnes it was different," Pocognoli said. "I knew before my first camp that he was different.

"The two other lads [Gray and Hackney] are young lads. It’s a long way. But if you wait too long, it might not be the right moment. In a year’s time, we will see.

“Right now, we have players in the squad who are performing well. It will always be up to them to be the priority.

"Because we’ve built things and we’ve had time with the ones who are here right now. But we are on it. We are always proactive in all of these situations.

"What is very exciting about those two names is that they are young players. That’s interesting. We have to look and manage the situation.”

Everton's Hackney made a couple of appearances for Scotland Under-21 side before going on to feature 13 times for the England Under-21s.

The 24-year-old now has to decide whether he will commit to England or Scotland, with Pocognoli feeling that the best route to convincing players like Hackney is by giving them a project to believe in.

“The best way to convince players is to show good football, show them they can come to us, enjoy it and be successful," the Scotland boss added.

“They have to feel when they leave a top club that they arrive here into top conditions and a top environment. That’s the best publicity we can offer, to show good football.”

Scotland will return to action against North Macedonia this evening, before they conclude the UEFA Nations League league phase with a game against Switzerland on Sunday.

#1785. Michael Carrick urged Manchester United to sign Chelsea star on his four-player shortlist

Michael Carrick urged Manchester United to sign Morgan Rogers ahead of Chelsea in the summer transfer window, according to reports.

Carrick was sacked by United on Thursday morning, while Mauricio Pochettino is expected to be appointed ahead of the team’s next Premier League game away to Liverpool on November 22.

After Sunday’s 4-4 draw at home to Aston Villa, United sit 18th in the Premier League and are already out of the Carabao Cup after they were beaten by Brighton in September.

Carrick was forced to contend with several injury headaches during his final weeks in charge as United were without Luke Shaw and a recognised striker with Benjamin Sesko sidelined until next year due to a shin injury.

United opted to focus on strengthening their midfield options in the summer and spent £155 million on signing Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Carlos Baleba.

According to The Telegraph, Carrick was ‘far from happy’ with United’s business in the summer transfer window and all four of his recommendations to the club’s hierarchy failed to materialise.

The report claims that Carrick wanted Rogers, who he had already managed at Middlesborough, and was ‘convinced’ that the 24-year-old wanted to make the move to United.

However, United’s hierarchy refused to enter a bidding war with Chelsea, who ended up signing Rogers in a £117m deal from Aston Villa.

Carrick also wanted United to sign Elliot Anderson, who moved to Manchester City for £116m, and had also recommended Mateus Fernandes, who joined Tottenham Hotspur for £85m after United refused to meet West Ham’s valuation.

#1784. Arsenal teach Chelsea a lesson in how to be champions

This is how champions are supposed to play and, although the Arsenal home support have not seen a team defend their place at the apex of English league football for two decades, they knew it when they saw it.

The chase was on for Mikel Arteta’s team within two minutes when Morgan Rogers, the man who might have moved to Arsenal this summer, put his new club Chelsea in the lead. So unfolded a thrilling 100 minutes of Premier League competition. Arsenal were the better team in terms of ambition and attack even if one could not discount Chelsea until the very last moment.

Others might have crumbled. That Chelsea did not will give Xabi Alonso hope for a team that did not feature the injured Moisés Caicedo and is now without the departed Enzo Fernández. Yet he will also recognise that his childhood friend from San Sebastián in the other dugout has created a side that treated the game, and their place in it, with an urgency that looks different. The first two minutes might have been ragged for Arsenal but after that they did not let the game happen to them.

Morgan Rogers fires Chelsea in front inside TWO minutes! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/ca8cqnT2Wm

Instead, Arteta’s players drove this contest, and the sequence of chances that came and went was dizzying at times. Their best players scored the two goals. First Kai Havertz, who now has three in four games this season, and then the captain Martin Ødegaard who dispatched what would be the winner.

"A spear through the heart of Chelsea!" Martin Odegaard puts Arsenal in front at the Emirates 🎯 pic.twitter.com/5deEQykjck

Ødegaard looked like the veteran of a title-winning season, and a deep run in the World Cup – an accomplished, shrewd performer in a midfield that was fought over ferociously all afternoon.

As for the game’s defining moment – it would be hard to overlook the feint from Havertz for the winning goal. It deceived the Chelsea players around him and created the channel for Christos Tzolis’s cross to reach Ødegaard. His goal was a close copy, in style and personnel, of the one he scored against Manchester City in the Community Shield but it was crowned by Havertz’s bluff. He shaped to take the ball and let it run under his foot at the last moment.

This was Chelsea’s first defeat in three – leaving only Arsenal and City with nine points from their first three games – although the seven goals conceded is the standout. For all the jet fuel in their attack they keep conceding. This was a much more exacting test than Fulham and Brighton previously, but even so. Alonso has introduced his preferred back three, often a back five, and it is a work in progress.

Arsenal have set the standard in that regard and they were uncompromising again. They did not replicate the errors that led to the Rogers goal and they pushed the limits at all times. Gabriel Magalhães kicked Emi Martínez in the head competing for a ball in the Chelsea area. Myles Lewis-Skelly went after João Pedro. Ben White and Roméo Lavia saw things differently in the first half. This Arsenal team does not shy away from those confrontations in the way their predecessors often did.

In fact, it was notable just how furiously Rogers reacted to Declan Rice when the two England team-mates converged as the Chelsea man charged off to join a late counter-attack. The bad feeling lingered even after the game when Rogers seemed unwilling to forgive. Rice had applied the minimum contact and the maximum cynicism to stop Rogers while the attention of referee Chris Kavanagh was elsewhere.

"He's FUMING Morgan Rogers!" 😳 pic.twitter.com/FciivEedvh

All that ringcraft was one thing, but it should be said that Arsenal were excellent in setting an attacking tempo that will be hell for any team to live with – especially at the Emirates. Havertz is now Arteta’s centre-forward of choice in the absence of a big summer acquisition. Viktor Gyökeres made a late substitute’s appearance – his first minutes of the season. The hierarchy is clear: last season’s great goalscoring hope is now back-up.

“Exceptional” was how Arteta described his team’s response to the early Rogers goal. They had twice failed to clear the ball in their own area when first Maxence Lacroix and then Jorrel Hato created the chance. Rogers’s right foot half-volley was not struck on the full, but it was placed perfectly inside the post with the necessary bounce and skip to mean David Raya never got behind it.

Arteta’s squad runs deep enough that in the closing stages he could relieve his midfield with two Spanish World Cup-winning substitutes – Martín Zubimendi and Mikel Merino. Then there was Noni Madueke on for Bukayo Saka, understudy and first-choice for club and country. This was not Saka’s day in the way it has been in the past, although a very promising shot of his was stopped by Martinez in the first half.

In the pounding that Chelsea took after they went into the lead, Riccardo Calafiori had an equaliser within minutes that was disallowed by VAR on an offside call. The left-back was the third in sequence to try to force the ball over the line from a Rice free-kick. Calafiori was successful, but the second of his team-mates to try, Ezri Konsa, had been offside when he connected.

For the equaliser it was Havertz, accelerating cautiously at first and then full-on with his left foot from the right-side. Ødegaard was well-placed to prevent Lacroix getting close but in truth the challenge never had the force required. Havertz’s shot was not totally convincing but then neither was Martinez’s attempt to save it – every bit as uncertain as Raya for the Chelsea goal.

A precise finish from Kai Havertz and Arsenal are level! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/DqL1MEX4zN

Chelsea had profited from the quick ball out to their right where Calafiori was often out of position in the left-back slot and Pedro Neto could cut in on his left foot. That seemed to be the sacrifice that Arteta was prepared to make in keeping the hammer on Chelsea. If Neto had not struck the post in one such escape in time added on at the end of the first half it might have been different.

Ødegaard struck what would be the winner early in the first half, and although Chelsea fizzed enough in the later stages it always felt as though it was Arsenal’s game. Raya came into his own in the 89th minute when Estêvão, a substitute, cut in from the right and hit a fierce shot that the goalkeeper pushed over. It was close in some ways – and in others not at all.

“It hurts. It hurts because a defeat has to hurt. It has been a very intense game with different moments for everything. We had chances to equalise. In the first half as well a couple of chances. Never happy if you lose.

“After we scored, there were 15-20 minutes where we had to defend too much and we were struggling a bit to get control. We then had better spells with the ball. Overall, it was a very tight, very intense game. We could do better with the second goal to conceded too early. The guys gave everything, tried everything. It has to hurt.

“It is about preparing the best possible way to compete the best possible way. You need to control the overloads on the right side. It is part of the game to have these actions. We continue. It is game three and this is going to be a long, long ride.”

"That's not sustainable" Daniel Sturridge reflects Chelsea's performance after the 2-1 defeat to Arsenal 💭 pic.twitter.com/3EMx88QLA0

"He's not the goalkeeper that won the World Cup" 🏆Jamie Carragher says Emi Martinez is not as quick or sharp as he once was 🧤 pic.twitter.com/SOp4XhoYIr

“I think the worrying thing for everybody else already is that [William] Saliba, who is genuinely world-class arguably, probably the best centre-back in world football, has not played a minute of football so far this season. And it does not look like anyone can score against them.

“There is a massive gulf between both teams; their XIs and the squads. It will take Chelsea a while to get to that level, if they can get there. But I thought Arsenal were fantastic today. We do not normally see Arsenal in these games, end-to-end, because they very rarely go behind. They are so strong defensively they do not need to get involved in those games.

“They still did not look like they were going to give too much away, even though they were bombing forwards and putting so many bodies in the opposition box.”

“It was a massive game with a tough opponent. It was really hard for us; we got there in the end. Our mentality is to keep fighting. Conceding early was not ideal but we reacted really well. We played well in the second half and got our reward. We showed our quality today. The result reflected that.”

“He is a really smart player and moves so well. He takes defenders attention. When he makes the run and I come from behind I am always free. It was a brilliant goal.”

“We knew Arsenal were the better team and they have proven that in this game. The question before today was, how close are Chelsea? And [Xabi] Alonso will be proud of what he has seen. There are obviously improvements to be made, but they gave it a right good go. A lot of very good things and they will be frustrated and disappointed, but they may potentially look back on this game as a good moment rather than as bad as it may feel right now.”

Gusto’s cross from the right is put behind by Konsa for a Chelsea corner out on the right. Neto clips it in but Arsenal head away. James then opts to shoot from range and his effort is blocked by Gabriel. That shot looked to be going on target but Raya may have had it covered anyway.

Palmer gets a shot away from the right side of the box but it is straight at Raya. Chelsea are just starting to wrestle back some momentum.

Two former teammates challenge each other as Konsa slides in to make a perfectly-timed challenge on Rogers. The home crowd loved that tackle from Konsa, who won that tackle fair and square.

Chelsea made Odegaard angry about two minutes before that goal. The Arsenal captain, who is a mild-mannered guy, was really unhappy with a tackle by James. They were exchanging some verbals afterwards, before Odegaard then ran away from James to score.

That’s five goals Chelsea have conceded in just over a game-and-a-half since Emi Martinez took over in goal. In fairness, that Odegaard goal wasn’t his fault.

Arsenal were forced to respond when Chelsea scored early but now it is on the visitors to see how they respond after falling behind.

For the first time this afternoon, Arsenal lead and it is a quality goal. Tzolis receives it out on the left and cuts inside onto his right. The first half is brought to an end and it is 1-1 going into the break at the Emirates.

The goal will not stand. Konsa was offside before Calafiori scored so Chelsea remain 1-0 up.

Hato brings Saka down not far outside the Chelsea penalty area and both Odegaard and Rice are standing over it. Chelsea have just three men in the wall. Rice is going to take...

It looked like Chelsea left four attackers upfield for that Arsenal corner. That’s one way of reducing the traffic in the six-yard box.

Bukayo Saka has arrived at a career crossroads. We will soon learn whether he is destined to be a good Arsenal player or if he will elevate himself to the level of Premier League, Champions League and England great.

This weekend Saka turns 25, an age when footballers typically enter their peak. Although his legendary status at Arsenal is secure as a title winner, the reaction to the champions’ transfer window suggests there is a general feeling that he can and should produce more to earn “world class” status.

Mikel Arteta is short of such an attacker. He spent the summer investigating whether players of Vinícius Júnior and Julián Alvarez’s calibre might add much-needed stardust to his front three. Failure to secure a big-name forward has led many to conclude that Arsenal’s title defence will be in the mould of their impressive, but cautious 1-0 victory at Aston Villa.

"It's another tough game"Ben White on coming up against Chelsea's front three 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/gfazGGNSA8

It is a relationship that Arteta has previously described as “deeper than just a friendship”. It started with skateboards and sand, as they made the daily journey to the beach to play tennis and football, and continued into their adult lives. When Alonso was playing for Liverpool and Arteta for Everton, there was a time when they both had flats on the fourth floor of the same building in the Albert Dock.

It is extraordinary that these two individuals – born just a few months apart – now find themselves in positions of such significance in English football. But it is not a coincidence. Throughout their lives, they have driven each other forward.

“This kid, he was maybe even crazier than me about football,” Alonso once said of Arteta and their shared childhood. “He was a little bit younger than me and my friends – just a few months maybe. But you know how you always push your ‘little friends’ at that age? Well, we tried, but he was a competitive monster.”

A personal opinion that no one asked for: Arsenal should have signed Joao Pedro last summer, when the Brazilian joined Chelsea for £60m. Arsenal bought Viktor Gyokeres instead, in a deal that could ultimately be more expensive, and there is no doubt which forward offers more to their team. Joao Pedro always seemed to cause problems for Arsenal’s defence when he played against them during his time at Brighton, and he has a flexibility and versatility that would have been perfect for Arteta’s system. Arsenal had twice explored the possibility of signing him over the years. It is surely a source of regret that they never became serious about it. So far this season, Joao Pedro has scored and assisted in both league games. Gyokeres, by contrast, has played zero minutes.

They have just got back under way in the second half on Merseyside and Manchester United have taken the lead against Everton through Bryan Mbeumo. You can follow the action from the Hill Dickinson here.

Will Ezri Konsa come into Arsenal’s starting lineup today? Today:Everton 0 Manchester United 0 HTArsenal vs Chelsea 4.30pm

Mikel Arteta insists Arsenal are “better equipped” for success this season, despite falling short in their attempts to add a top-class attacker. Arsenal have allowed four forward players to leave this summer and brought in one, Greece winger Christos Tzolis.

The departures of Gabriel Martinelli, Leandro Trossard, Gabriel Jesus and Ethan Nwaneri (on loan) have raised concerns among supporters that the champions lack firepower. Moves for Morgan Rogers, Vinicius Junior and Julian Alvarez did not come to fruition. Arteta, though, feels Arsenal are stronger now than at the end of last season following a summer in which they added midfielder Bruno Guimarães and defender Ezri Konsa.

“We are better equipped,” said Arteta, who faces Rogers and close friend Xabi Alonso. “We have more players available than the start of last season. We have increased the quality and we have increased the leadership, which is very important.”

Asked specifically about the attack, he added: “Yeah, but that’s another question. We have to prove in that particular position whether we are better or not. Let’s see. We need to play. I don’t like to make assumptions.

“It’s not just the responsibility of those players, it’s the team and the dynamic. We have multiple options to play there with different profiles. It’s human nature. When you talk to people and you ask: ‘Ok, what is on your bucket list?’ Sometimes we forget the reverse bucket list, which are the things you already have that are incredible. It’s very important to value what we have, what we have created together. The ambition is great, but [don’t] lose perspective to what we already have which is amazing.”

Two sides with 100% records meet in a London derby in north London as defending champions Arsenal host Chelsea at the Emirates. Arsenal have wins over Coventry and Aston Villa to their name whilst Chelsea have beaten Fulham and Brighton.

Arsenal could make it three wins from three to start the season, a feat they have only achieved once in the last 21 seasons. They have lost just one of their last 29 Premier League London derbies. Mikel Arteta comes up against his childhood friend Xabi Alonso today.

“Really happy for him [Alonso],” Arteta said. “It is incredible because obviously we have the history we have together, the same with Andoni [Iraola]. To be facing each other at such a level and with the responsibility we have managing some of the top clubs in the country is a really beautiful thing to experience. Now it will be tougher to meet because of the schedule we both have but that friendship will go for many years. We shared some great moments but now it is the competition and when you face each other, you know what happens.”

Chelsea were involved in late drama on transfer deadline day. They were on the verge of signing midfielder Lamine Camara from Monaco only to see that deal fall through at the last minute. After being linked with a move away throughout the summer, Chelsea did in the end sell Enzo Fernandez to Manchester City for a joint Premier League transfer record fee of £125m.

“In football, many things happen and you need to be prepared for everything,” Chelsea boss Alonso said. “With Enzo, we have had conversations, but always with respect for what he has done for the club. It has been great, we are thankful, but it is time to move forward. We take all the decisions together. We are responsible for them, we work together with every decision, big and small.

“We knew that, ultimately, the last goal is to have the best for the team, the best for the squad, the best for daily work here. We want to build a good spirit, a good team, and we have always taken decisions thinking we want to reach that. We have the squad we have. We have a lot of big personalities, players with a lot of quality in all the different positions, different lines and now we are ready to go.”

Arsenal won this fixture 2-1 last season, with William Saliba and Jurrien Timber earning Mikel Arteta’s side three points on their way to the title. Arsenal are unbeaten in their last nine Premier League matches against Chelsea.

Team news from the Emirates to follow shortly.

#1783. England player ratings vs Croatia as Harry Kane scores on record-breaking appearance

Harry Kane celebrated his record-breaking 126th England cap with the winning goal as the Three Lions won 2-1 against Croatia in the Nations League.

After a slow start from the hosts, Thomas Tuchel’s side opened the scoring when Morgan Rogers bundled Jude Bellingham’s cross home from close range.

A mistake from Jarell Quansah allowed Petar Sucic to equalise from a corner after the break.

But the Bayer Leverkusen defender made amends just moments later, winning a penalty from a corner, which Kane stepped up to convert and secure England their place in the Nations League quarter-final.

Metro was at Wembley to rate England’s performances on a historic night for their captain.

#1782. Real Madrid's Endrick faces Donyell Malen dilemma over Roma loan

By Naim Beneddra | 13 Nov 2026 17:58

Real Madrid forward Endrick could find an attractive route back to regular football at Roma in January, but the remarkable form of former Aston Villa attacker Donyell Malen raises questions over the Brazilian's potential role under Gian Piero Gasperini.

The 20-year-old has struggled for opportunities since returning from his successful loan spell at Lyon, managing just 141 minutes across seven appearances for Real Madrid this season.

Roma remain interested in signing him on loan when the transfer window reopens, having already attempted to secure his services during the summer before Jose Mourinho blocked the move.

However, a potential switch to the Italian capital presents an intriguing sporting dilemma. Malen has established himself as one of Serie A's most productive forwards, scoring eight goals in his first 10 league appearances of the 2026-27 campaign.

For Endrick, whose main priority is securing consistent playing time, joining a team with such an established attacking figure could carry a familiar risk.

Malen has been outstanding since joining Roma from Aston Villa in January 2026, scoring 14 goals in 18 Serie A appearances during the second half of last season.

The Netherlands international has maintained that impressive form under Gasperini, adding eight league goals and four Champions League strikes this term.

His performances have made him a central figure in Roma's attacking system, with the Italian side emerging as genuine contenders near the top of Serie A after finishing third last season.

The competition for Endrick would therefore be considerable, particularly if he arrived expecting to operate as the team's first-choice centre-forward.

Yet an analysis published by Brazilian outlet Trivela suggests that Gasperini's tactical approach could offer the Real Madrid youngster opportunities beyond the traditional number nine position.

Roma generally operate with three central defenders, attacking wing-backs and two supporting forwards behind a central striker.

Their emphasis on aggressive pressing, direct attacking movements and exploiting spaces behind opposition defences could suit Endrick's explosive acceleration and ability to finish quickly.

Rather than competing exclusively with Malen, the Brazilian could potentially operate alongside him as a second striker, receiving possession between the lines before driving towards goal.

Malen's movement across the forward line would also provide opportunities for Endrick to attack spaces created by the Dutchman's positioning.

Such an arrangement would require tactical adjustments from Gasperini, however, and there has been no indication that the Roma manager has guaranteed Endrick a particular role.

The Italian club also possess other attacking options, including Paulo Dybala, Matias Soule and Rodrigo Mora, meaning the youngster would still face competition even if deployed behind Malen.

Interestingly, the two forwards were both on the scoresheet when Real Madrid secured a dramatic 4-3 Champions League victory over Roma on October 14.

Malen struck twice for the hosts, while Endrick came off the bench to score Madrid's equaliser before Antonio Rudiger completed the comeback.

Endrick's situation at Real Madrid has become increasingly difficult despite his encouraging performances during last season's loan at Lyon.

The former Palmeiras youngster scored eight goals in 21 appearances in France, demonstrating how regular involvement could accelerate his development.

His limited opportunities under Mourinho have since prompted renewed speculation about another temporary departure.

Speaking while on international duty with Brazil earlier this week, Endrick acknowledged that his immediate priority was simply to play more regularly.

"I just want to play. I want to be happy, to help my teammates... to score goals and provide assists, just as I did at Lyon, which was one of the best things that's ever happened to me and one of the happiest times of my life," he told reporters.

"I don't know what will happen in January. That's in God's hands. I'm only 20 and I'll see what happens. I just ask to do what's best for my career."

Roma's interest remains genuine, with La Repubblica reporting this week that the club are monitoring the Brazilian's situation as they consider January attacking reinforcements.

However, Sporting Lisbon have also emerged as serious contenders for Endrick's signature, with former Lyon manager Paulo Fonseca reportedly keen on a reunion.

That connection could prove significant, given the improvement Endrick showed during their previous spell together in France.

Meanwhile, Mourinho's previous decision to reject Roma's approach remains another obstacle, with Real Madrid yet to approve a January departure.

Roma can offer Champions League football, a competitive Serie A environment and a tactical system that appears suited to Endrick's attacking qualities.

Whether those advantages outweigh the prospect of competing with Malen for minutes could be crucial if the Italian club succeed in reopening negotiations.

For a player who has started just once for Real Madrid this season, the possibility of playing alongside Roma's leading scorer may be appealing, but any January decision will also depend on how regularly Gasperini can accommodate him.

#1778. Sheffield Wednesday 3 Plymouth 0: A win's a win as Owls get Dave Challinor up and running without sparkling

After six games without a win and back-to-back cup defeats to start Challinor's managerial reign, it did not matter how they beat Plymouth Argyle, just that they did.

A 3-0 win with goals from the excellent Billy Mitchell, Davis Keillor-Dunn and a brilliant individual goal from Di'Shon Bernard flattered Wednesday.

None of the home fans in the 29,228 will have cared.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

With only a patchy schedule in international week, they are back in the League One play-off places and above Plymouth on goal difference.

Wednesday were very poor in the first half until taking the lead just as it came to the end. They matched the Pilgrims in the second half without blowing them away.

The atmosphere for Challinor's first home league game was pretty flat for the first hour, with the team failing to get the Hillsborough crowd excited.

The Owls' first-half football was as low-key as Challinor's introduction to the crowd, Plymouth's football not as bright as their luminous orange kit and certainly not on a par with the annoying pitchside advertising hoardings, but much better than Wednesday's in the opening 44 minutes.

Starting in a shape which flitted between 4-2-3-1 and 3-2-4-1 as Sil Swinkels tucked in and Yan Valery pushed on in possession, the Owls struggled to keep the ball and therefore pose any attacking threat to a team who, like them, have promotion ambitions and a long injury list.

Jaden Heskey being caught on the ball in the ninth minute summed up the hosts' slackness and he was fortunate Callum Slattery tracked back and made a penalty-area tackle which had to be perfectly timed.

Roman Curtis had a shot saved by the fit-again Joe Lumley in the tenth minute after Xavier Amaechi nutmegged Swinkels in the build up. The ball was bundled behind for a corner Lumley flapped at but Will Evans could only cushion his volley from it into the side netting.

A lovely ball from Malachi Boateng found Bradley Ibrahim, but Lumley came off his line to save. Evans shot at the goalkeeper when picked out.

Bernard was hassled into an error in the 37th minute but made up for it with some good defending when the ball came in, just as he made a good recovery tackle when Amaechi threatened to force his way through.

In between time, Ibrahim missed a woeful chance, thrashing at fresh air rather than the ball Amaechi laid on for him. The far-post header Amaechi put wide in the 63rd minute would equal it for wastefulness.

That said, Plymouth had a reprieve in the 17th minute when Curtis planted his studs into the chest of Jamal Lowe, but only received a yellow card.

As half-time approached, Wednesday had only had a couple of half-chances, Mitchell's first-time wall pass finding Keillor-Dunn on the counter-attack but his ball to Barry Bannan giving Wes Harding the chance to make a brilliant slide tackle.

Slattery's excellent pass found Mitchell in the 35th minute, but, forced wide, he could only win a corner.

But the Owls delivered right at the end of the half.

Bernard thought he had scored from a corner, only for Ibrahim to nod his goalbound effort over the bar and when former Owls loanee touched the next one to Mitchell, his shot took a big deflection on its way in.

The sides matched each other chance for chance at the start of the second half.

A quick throw-in set up Keillor-Dunn for a shot that was blocked, and when Plymouth counter-attacked, the same fate befell Ibrakim's effort.

With the crowd sensing the part they had to play, just after the hour Keillor-Dunn released Lowe to weave his way through and force a save. The ball came back to Keillor-Dunn, who really ought to have hit the target. So should Amaechi with his header a minute later.

Louie Barry had an early chance to mark his first appearance since September 1 with a goal, but leant back on his shot.

Two goals in as many minutes put the doubts out of minds, though.

The first came when Plymouth defended a Slattery free-kick awfully, and Keillor-Dunn popped up to poke hme a centre-forward's goal, his sixth of the season.

If he was an entirely predictable scorer, Bernard was not.

The centre-back loves to barrel forward from time to time but it rarely ends with a finish as good as the one he hit in off a post after what turned out to be a one-two in his own half with Boateng's sliding tackle and just carrying on.

It papered over a few cracks, but no matter.

Sheffield Wednesday: Lumley; Valery, Bernard, Cooper, Swinkels; Mitchell, Heskey; Slattery, Bannan (Barry 72), J Lowe (Palmer 85); Keillor-Dunn (Gray 85).

Unused substitutes: Santos, Trueman, Weaver, Thornton.

Plymouth Argyle: Cooper; Harding, MacKenzie (Irow 63), Hartridge; Curtis, Boateng, White (Oseni 77), Ross; Amaechi, Ibrahim (Watts 63); Evans.

Unused substitutes: Storer, Campbell, Mwaro, Maund.

Arsenal reportedly have identified AC Milan attacker Alphadjo Cisse as a potential transfer target.

However, they ultimately failed in their pursuit of the Brazilian, who decided to sign a new long-term contract with Los Blancos.

With that in mind, Arsenal are likely to revisit their pursuit of attacking reinforcements in the upcoming transfer windows.

According to Tuttomercatoweb, the Gunners have identified Milan's Cisse as a potential target for their future transfer business.

The Premier League leaders are said to be showing 'strong interest' in Cisse, along with Brighton & Hove Albion.

The report also claims other clubs have made enquiries about the possibility of signing the Milan youngster.

The Italian giants are said to value Cisse in the region of €50m (£41.8m) to €60m (£50m) for an attacker who is under contract until June 2030.

Cisse started his senior career with Hellas Verona before joining Serie B side Catanzaro on loan in the summer of 2025.

After being impressed with Cisse's performances, Milan swooped in to secure his signature at the start of February before loaning him back to Catanzaro.

Having since linked up with the Rossoneri, the highly-rated talent has quickly adapted to life as a top-flight footballer, having netted five goals in Serie A appearances.

The 20-year-old also scored his first senior hat-trick in a 4-0 win over Red Bull Salzburg in last month's Europa League clash.

Cisse, who recently earned a call-up to Roberto Mancini's Italy squad, has primarily been used as an attacking midfielder by Ruben Amorim this season, but he is capable of playing slightly deeper, out wide and even as a striker.

#1771. Barcelona's Deco targets Brazilian first-team star in five-year plan

By Naim Beneddra | 13 Nov 2026 18:18

Barcelona's new partnership with Brazilian academy Sfera FC comes with an ambitious target: developing at least one player capable of reaching the Catalan club's first team within the next five years.

The objective was revealed by Sfera co-founder and chief executive Gustavo Aranha in an exclusive interview with Trivela, offering fresh insight into the agreement recently negotiated by Barcelona sporting director Deco.

The two clubs announced a five-year collaboration earlier this month, giving Barcelona preferential access to emerging Brazilian talents while allowing young players to experience the training environment at La Masia.

However, Aranha has now explained that the project extends well beyond identifying potential transfer targets, with Sfera hoping to establish a direct pathway from its academy in Sao Paulo to Barcelona's senior squad.

"Beyond that, the main objective is to have at least one player developed by Sfera playing in Barcelona's first team within five years," Aranha told Trivela.

It is an ambition set by the Brazilian club rather than a guarantee from Barcelona, whose agreement contains no obligation to sign players or promote them to the senior side.

The agreement originated from a visit Deco made to Sfera's training facilities in May, although the former Barcelona midfielder was already familiar with the organisation before becoming the club's sporting director.

Aranha explained that the visit helped transform their existing relationship into formal negotiations, eventually resulting in a five-season contract.

Established in 2021, Sfera specialises in developing young footballers rather than operating as a conventional professional club.

Its academy currently works with players from under-11 to under-19 level, and the organisation has no intention of establishing a senior team.

"Our partners and I never wanted to have a traditional football club. We wanted to build the best player development process in Brazil," Aranha explained.

Barcelona's involvement provides a significant opportunity for that model, particularly given the competition among European clubs to identify promising Brazilian youngsters before their market values increase.

Under the agreement, Barcelona will receive priority when assessing players developed by Sfera, with the two organisations working together to identify individuals suited to the Catalans' sporting requirements.

Nevertheless, the Spanish giants are under no contractual obligation to complete any transfers.

Aranha also confirmed that the clubs deliberately rejected the idea of setting a minimum number of players to be sent to Barcelona each season.

Such a requirement could have resulted in youngsters being recommended before they were ready, while also potentially restricting opportunities if Sfera produced an especially promising generation.

The partnership does not prevent the Brazilian academy from maintaining relationships with other clubs, either.

"The Barcelona partnership is not about them coming to Sfera to teach us how to develop players according to their methodology," Aranha added.

"They want Sfera to continue doing its work, using the institutional relationship to enhance and showcase our players."

For Deco, the arrangement offers a more direct connection to a Brazilian development programme without Barcelona needing to establish or operate their own academy in the country.

One of the most distinctive aspects of the agreement concerns the possibility of Sfera players making repeated visits to Barcelona before any permanent transfer is considered.

Rather than inviting youngsters to Spain for a conventional trial, the clubs intend to create a gradual process of assessment and adaptation.

Sfera will recommend players based on their development and individual characteristics, while Barcelona's coaching staff will assess whether they meet the club's requirements.

Selected youngsters could then spend several weeks training at La Masia before returning to Brazil with specific areas of their game to improve.

"It's not about a definitive trial where a player goes there and stays, but about building an adaptation process through several visits," Aranha explained.

"That way, Barcelona get to know the player closely, and we understand which areas we need to focus on developing when he returns."

This approach is designed to prepare youngsters for the demands of European football before they face the additional pressures of a permanent move abroad.

It could be particularly valuable when players approach the transition to Barcelona's under-19 or reserve teams.

The agreement also includes exchanges between coaching staff, allowing Sfera employees to observe La Masia's training methods and incorporate relevant lessons into their work in Brazil.

Aranha stressed that the Brazilian club would retain its own identity, rather than becoming a Barcelona satellite academy.

Sfera's development model places considerable importance on education, emotional development and individual support alongside conventional technical and physical preparation.

Players undergo weekly video analysis sessions, while the academy also aims to develop their decision-making and understanding of the game.

For Barcelona, the potential reward is early access to youngsters who have already experienced the club's footballing environment.

For Sfera, the ultimate measure of success would be seeing one of those players progress through the academy system and eventually represent the senior side.

The five-year agreement includes the possibility of an extension, although Aranha believes the relationship should ultimately be judged by the quality of the players developed and the opportunities created.

No specific youngster has yet been identified as the potential beneficiary of that first-team ambition, but the partnership gives Barcelona a structured route to monitor the next generation of Brazilian talent long before a permanent transfer becomes necessary.
