Kobbie Mainoo impressed again in central midfield and Carrick was able to substitute a number of his best players early with the derby in mind, as well as resting Luke Shaw entirely.

Goals from Matheus Cunha, Bruno Fernandes and Benjamin Sesko in the first half killed the game as a contest before Lisandro Martínez scored a fourth with just over 20 minutes remaining.

Matheus Cunha opens the scoring for Manchester United with his first ever Champions League goal 🏄📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ZDQBbEfizq

“It’s nice to keep a clean sheet and obviously win the game,” Carrick said. “Some of the football we played was really good – dangerous on the transition. The result looks comfortable, but it wasn’t always like that but we did a lot of good things.

United probably could not have asked for a softer return to Champions League football. Atlético Madrid at the Wanda Metropolitano next month will certainly be a very different beast, but it was a rewarding first 45 minutes all the same that paved the way for Carrick to ring the changes ahead of the derby.

Already leading 1-0, two goals shortly before the interval changed the complexion of the game and effectively extinguished any flickering hopes Sabah had of a gargantuan upset.

Founded just nine years ago, Sabah had navigated four qualifying rounds that began on July 7 just to reach this stage.

Throw in the fact Valdas Dambrauskas, their Lithuanian manager, got his break in coaching with the Manchester United Soccer Schools 20 years ago, and it is quite the heartwarming tale.

But there is not much sentiment at this level and, given time and space, United punished their inexperience and carelessness.

Carrick will not read too much into the performance. City will be an entirely different proposition and it will be interesting to see whether he goes for a two-man midfield with Bruno Fernandes deployed as an advanced No 10, or perhaps operates with a midfield three and adjusts his attack.

Either way, Mainoo will be central to the game plan.

It is hard to believe the England midfielder missed most of pre-season after reporting back late following the World Cup, because he has barely missed a beat in his last three outings, even if his team-mates have not always hummed to his tune.

There is so much to like about Mainoo. His manipulation of space, how he never looks under duress, even when hounded, and his vision on the ball. There was one lovely angled ball over the top here, after United had worked the space well, that released Fernandes in behind. His cross was cut out before Sesko could tap in.

Mainoo’s work off the ball has improved enormously, too. There were numerous instances here of him making a timely intervention or nicking the ball away at the right moment to recover possession.United have spent £155m reconfiguring their midfield, but Mainoo will be a constant. “He’s a fantastic player, it’s pretty obvious to see,” Carrick said. “He has a massive influence on our games. He is a real joy to have, he wants to improve, he wants to listen and it’s great to see.”

Kobbie Mainoo completed 81/83 passes, 6/6 accurate long balls and 10 passes into final third on his full Champions League debut ⭐️ pic.twitter.com/NK9BIGvc4m

It will certainly be interesting to see how Carrick’s new-look midfield shapes up against City’s own revamped one in the form of Elliot Anderson, Enzo Fernández and Ayyoub Bouaddi.

“There are some good connections and we have played some good football through the middle of the pitch,” Carrick added. “A lot of it is on wavelength and understanding of where each other wants the ball. We haven’t had the perfect start but there are really good signs.”

Carrick was suitably confident to withdraw Youri Tielemans at half-time and bring on Mason Mount, who was having a good pre-season before his familiar injury jinx hit, and he will have been pleased to see Sesko on the scoresheet again. “He definitely offers a different kind of threat,” Carrick said. “There are not many who can give us what Ben does with his physicality, playing on the last line. It’s great to have him back.”

Sesko’s goal, rounding the goalkeeper to slot home from Bryan Mbeumo’s pass after line-breaking balls from Mainoo and Fernandes, capped off a quick-fire three minutes when Sabah were unpicked. Before then, Cunha had picked out Tielemans’s burst into the penalty area, from where he pulled the ball back for Fernandes to coolly finish.

Benjamin Šeško rounds the goalkeeper to make it three for Manchester United 🔄📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/tnslugsmZM

Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans combine to double Manchester United's lead ✌️📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nZnkwLWJ00

United had taken the lead when Kaheem Parris paid the price for a misplaced pass straight to Mbeumo, from which the ball was moved at pace between Sesko, Fernandes and Patrick Dorgu to tee up Cunha to score.

Dorgu was starting here at left-back with Shaw rested with one eye on City. It was an early glimpse of how Carrick is going to have to manage the minutes of his only recognised senior left-back, who is not going to be able to play every few days.

Carrick prefers Dorgu further up the pitch and it remains to be seen if he trusts the Dane at left-back in bigger games than this.

With City having played in Porto on Tuesday and had a little extra rest time, the United manager will have been pleased he got the chance to withdraw several key players early. He was even able to give a rare run-out to Joshua Zirkzee and it was the Dutchman who helped to force the fourth goal.

Lisandro Martínez pounces on a defensive mistake from Sabah to make it four 🫣📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/eTAYgMmV9Q

Fernandes’s quick free-kick caught out Sabah and Zirkzee back-heeled the ball goalwards. It bounced off Aden McCarthy and from there goalkeeper Stas Pokatilov got himself in a dreadful spin, unable to locate the ball by which point Martínez had blasted it in from a yard out.

“Nice to have a clean sheet and obviously win the game. Some of our attacking play was fantastic. We were dangerous in transition, defended well in the most part. The result looks comfortable but it was not as easy as that. Kobbie [Mainoo] is a fantastic player, it is pretty obvious to see. He has a massive influence on our game and a real joy to have. Through the middle of the pitch, we have played some good football at times and we can get better. There are some good signs which we have shown tonight. The confidence is there, like at Everton on Sunday for large spells, just took a hit there at the end with the result. It is always nice to win. Another big one on Sunday.”

The final whistle is blown at Old Trafford and Manchester United claim a 4-0 victory on their return to the Champions League. Goals from Cunha, Fernandes, Sesko and Martinez give Michael Carrick’s side three points in their opening game of the competition. Debutants Sabah return home with nothing and no goals, despite some decent chances to get a goal.

A number of empty seats at Old Trafford are becoming visible as some home fans have seen enough, knowing their side is going to win.

Sabah have had a few chances to come away from their Champions League debut with a goal but have wasted some great chances, including one just now. Mickels delivers a lovely cross from the left, which perfectly picks out Mbina, but his header goes just over the bar.

Mickels wasted a glorious chance in the first half and he comes close to goal a now but drags his shot just wide of the far post from the left side of the box.

How on earth have the officials missed that one? Cunha catches Almeida on the leg and it should be at least a booking but the officials do not see it, despite the linesman being not far away. Cunha is very lucky as that was a nasty challenge.

Sabah would love to at the very least send their travelling fans back to Azerbaijan with a goal on their Champions League debut. You do wonder how different the game could have been had Mickels not missed a sitter that would have seen Sabah make it 1-1.

Michael Carrick is going to make his final two changes of the night as youngsters Lacey and Amass come on.

A bit of a soft goal for Sabah to concede. Fernandes clips in a free-kick into the Sabah box which picks out the run of Zirkzee. The Dutchman’s backheel is blocked and Sabah should then deal with the danger. However, Sabah make an absolute mess of things and their keeper Pokatilov has no idea where the ball is, allowing Martinez to nick in and smash the ball into the net.

Lisandro Martínez pounces on a defensive mistake from Sabah to make it four 🫣📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/eTAYgMmV9Q

Lepinjica is the first Sabah player into the book tonight for a cynical trip on Mount.

Zirkzee, only just on the pitch, shoots from range but it is straight down the throat of Pokatilov.

Puchacz takes the free-kick from just over 25 yards out and strikes it well but the effort is just off target.

Perhaps with the Manchester derby on Sunday in mind, Michael Carrick is going to make a double change. Zirkzee and Santos replace Sesko and Mainoo.

Dorgu is the first player into the book tonight. Lepinjica spots the run of Parris into the right channel and plays a clever pas forward. Dorgu cynically brings Parris down and is rightly booked.

The visitors are making a change as Parris is replaced by Isaev.

Manchester United come close to a fourth and Cunha his second. The home side work it well near the Sabah penalty area with a couple of clever flicks and passes before Cunha has an effort saved by Pokatilov to his left.

Mazraoui receives it out in space on the right and cuts inside onto his left. He comes across the face of the penalty area before getting his shot away but his effort is off target.

Sabah are enjoying a decent spell of possession but have not yet threatened Lammens’ goal in this second half.

Is Yoro lucky? Mickels appeared to turn him not far outside the Manchester United penalty area but Yoro is not penalised. It did on first viewing look like a foul and would have been at least a yellow card.

We are back under way at Old Trafford. How quickly might Michael Carrick make changes with Sunday’s Manchester derby in mind? Well, he has made one change at the break as Mount replaces Tielemans. It is Mount’s first appearance of the season. Sabah have brought on Mbina at the break.

Those two goals late in the half completely change the complexion of the game and Michael Carrick’s half-time team talk. Good first 45 minutes back in the Champions League for United.

The first half is brought to an end and Manchester United are cruising towards victory on their return to the Champions League. It has all gone wrong for Sabah.

That is game, set and match before half-time at Old Trafford as the dam has burst for Sabah. Sesko is played in behind by Mbeumo and is one-on-one with Pokatilov. Sesko takes it around Pokatilov before putting it into the empty net.

Benjamin Šeško rounds the goalkeeper to make it three for Manchester United 🔄📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/tnslugsmZM

Michael Carrick’s side have their second of the night not long before half-time and it is a well-taken goal. Cunha, from the left side of the box, plays it inside to Tielemans. The Belgian takes one touch before, on the turn, playing it back into the path of Fernandes, who finds the net with a first-time finish.

Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans combine to double Manchester United's lead ✌️📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nZnkwLWJ00

Fernandes has an effort from the edge of the Sabah box but blazes his effort high over the bar.

That’s a warning there for United. Fernandes gives the ball away in the middle with a heavy touch and Sabah break through the tall, languid figure of Lepinjica. Parris’ cross loops the far post where Mickels should have done better than steer an inviting header into the side netting. Bit of a let off for Carrick’s side.

Sabah should be level as they miss a sitter. Parris, from the right side of the box, clips a cross to the back post that picks out Mickels. He should score but puts his header into the side netting. That should have been the equaliser for Sabah.

Dorgu clips in a cross from the left side of the box and picks out Sesko, whose hooked first-time effort goes just wide.

Half an hour in and United have been in command. It’s not scintillating but they warrant their lead and punished a misplaced pass by Parris brutally. Mainoo is orchestrating the game in the middle of the pitch. Best player on the park so far.

Parris’ shot from the edge of the box takes a deflection and goes behind for a corner. It is wasted though by Sabah as the inswinger is easily caught by Lammens.

Tielemans steps in with a crucial interception inside his own box to deny Mickels the chance of a shot on goal.

The Brazilian has his first Champions League goal but it is gifted by Sabah. The visitors are threatening a counter-attack but Parris inexplicably gives the ball away on halfway with a dreadful pass across the pitch. The ball is then moved out to the left, where Dorgu crosses. He picks out Cunha, whose first-time effort with his side foot hits the Sabah keeper Pokatilov and goes into the net. A sense of frustration had been growing inside Old Trafford but Sabah have rather gifted Manchester United the opener there.

Matheus Cunha opens the scoring for Manchester United with his first ever Champions League goal 🏄📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ZDQBbEfizq

Sabah give it away inside their own half and Manchester United flood forward towards the Sabah penalty area. Mbuemo drives forward and cuts inside onto his preferred left foot before getting his shot away from the edge of the box but it is straight at Pokatilov.

That is outstanding defensive work from Dasdamirov. Mainoo plays a quite sensational first-time ball in behind into the right channel to pick out the run of Fernandez. The Manchester United captain has Sesko waiting in the middle for the cross but Dasdamirov steps in with an absolutely essential interception or else Sesko would have had a tap-in.

Sabah need to be careful as now a few times they have been caught in possession deep in their own territory.

Cunha sends in a corner from the left that threatens to go in at the far corner but Sabah keeper Pokatilov catches it near his own line.

Sabah are making their Champions League debut and so too tonight are Cesc Fabregas’ Como, who have just taken the lead at home against RB Leipzig. Manchester United will travel to Como in late October on matchday three. Manchester United play RB Leipzig at home on matchday six.

Sabah have to negotiate a couple of Manchester United corners in quick succession and they do so. The visitors’ starting XI tonight has a very international feel to it:

Sabah FC have named a starting XI featuring 11 different nationalities 🌍🇰🇿 Stas Pokatilov🇩🇿 Akim Zedadka🇦🇿 Rahman Dashdamirov🇿🇦 Aden McCarthy🇵🇱 Tymoteusz Puchacz🇺🇿 Umarali Rakhmonaliev🇭🇷 Ivan Lepinjica🇯🇲 Kaheem Parris🇷🇸 Veljko Simic🇳🇬 Christian Nwachukwu🇷🇼 Joy-Lance… pic.twitter.com/ih5Sf1aeie

Mazraoui, despite starting at right-back, has already had three shots in the game. Two have been outside the box that have been blocked and the latest hits the side netting from the right side of the penalty area.

Mazraoui plays a pass forward into Cunha on the right side of the box and the Brazilian tries to beat Pokatilov at the near post but the Sabah keeper makes the save and pushes it around the post for a corner.

Sabah are able to clear their lines from Mbeumo’s delivery.

Sabah seem content to take risks on the ball deep inside their own half and play out from the back. Will that be a masterstroke or is it asking for trouble?

Sabah make their first foray into the Manchester United penalty area and there are appeals for handball. It did hit Dorgu’s hand but it was right down by his side and that is not a deliberate handball. Sabah do win a corner, which Dorgu heads away.

Sesko, fresh off what he thought was going to be the winner at Everton on Sunday, has been given the nod to start up top for the home side tonight. He is very close to closing the Sabah goalkeeper Pokatilov down inside his own six-yard box and that was nearly a horrific moment for the Champions League debutants a matter of minutes into their debut in this competition.

Sabah started their journey through the qualifying rounds of this comeptition back in the early parts of July so they have already played quite a number of games so far this season, in comparison to Manchester United’s three competitive fixtures coming into tonight.

As has been the case at every Champions League game this week, there is a moment silence to remember the victims of the recent deadly floods in Nepal.

We are under way at Old Trafford. Manchester United, three-time winners of this trophy, return to the Champions League whilst Sabah make their debut in the competition.

It’s 1,003 days since the Champions League anthem has been heard at Old Trafford and, to be honest, it feels longer. There are about 500 Sabah fans here tonight.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel at Old Trafford and we are moments away from kick-off. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this evening:

Michael Carrick has made four changes for Sabah to the team that drew 2-2 against Everton. Benjamin Sesko is given his first start of the season with Marcus Rashford dropping to the bench. Luke Shaw was given an additional rest day on Wednesday and is left out of the squad. It makes sense with Sunday’s derby against Manchester City to come but it’s an early glimpse of the delicate balance Carrick will have to strike with his only recognised senior left back this season. Shaw can’t be expected to play every few days given his history of injury problems.

It looks like Patrick Dorgu will be operating at left back against Sabah. This is United’s 300th fixture in the European Cup, including qualifiers. On the subject of qualifiers, Sabah became only the sixth side to navigate four qualifying rounds to reach the European Cup proper, with their campaign starting back on July 7. That was the same day Argentina beat Egypt in the last 16 of the World Cup. The Azerbaijan club were only formed nine years ago so have had quite the ascent since.

At 8pm on Thursday night, Manchester United will kick a ball in the Champions League for the first time in three seasons.

It must mark the start of a permanent return to Europe’s premier club competition. If United are serious about once again challenging for the Premier League title and building a £2bn stadium, that must be the way forward.

This is only the seventh time in 13 campaigns that United have been in the Champions League and the implications have been significant.

Presenting your Champions League Reds 📋❤️‍🔥

Manchester United make their return to the Champions League as they host tournament debutants Sabah of Azerbaijan on matchday one at Old Trafford. It will be the first time that Manchester United have faced an Azerbaijani side in European competition.

Manchester United have one win, one loss and one draw to their name in their opening three Premier League games. They were seconds away from winning their second game of the season on Sunday but conceded a late equaliser at Everton. They last featured in the Champions League during the 2023/24 season, when they were eliminated in the group stage, and have won just one of their last nine games in the competition.

“It means an awful lot [to be back in the Champions League],” Manchester United boss Michael Carrick said. “Challenging yourself against the elite, the very best. This football club has been used to being the best. It is not something you can take for granted. We missed out on it for a number of years and now we are back. It is where we expect to be without getting ahead of ourselves. We have made huge steps to make it in, now it is about pushing into the next chapter and evolution if the squad and this is certainly where we want to be.

“I do not think it is a case of if we get to a certain stage it is a success and if we do not it is not. We have to embrace the new challenge that we are facing as a group and push to what we can push to. If we get further down the line in this competition then who knows? I am not writing anything off. But we are taking it step by step and we certainly are not getting ahead of ourselves. We have got a squad that is strong enough to compete.”

Sabah make their Champions League debut having been founded just eight years ago in September 2017. Back in April, they secured the Azerbaijan top-flight title for the first time in their history and also won the Azerbaijan Cup in May. They earned a spot in the Champions League group stages after beating Hapoel Be’er Sheva 6-4 on aggregate. In the previous three seasons, they have tried to reach the group stages of the Europa and Conference Leagues but failed to do so. They have won all three leagues thus far, including a 5-0 home win over Zira last Saturday.

#1661. Rabiot praises Donnarumma’s performance and admits France need time: “Part of the journey”

Last night, AC Milan’s Adrien Rabiot returned to San Siro – alongside Mike Maignan – as the French national team were beaten by Italy.

There was talk in the last international break that Zinedine Zidane wasn’t a huge fan of Rabiot. Yet, the midfielder was awarded the armband at San Siro. With this, a statement was made that the Frenchman needed to impress, but the trust was there for him to do so.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Whilst he could not lead his team to victory, though, there were several positives to take from the game, with one outlet giving him a 7/10.

It’s a frustrating defeat for Les Bleus – and a rare one for Rabiot and Maignan at San Siro – but it shows that they still have a lot to do with Zidane. After all, it’s better for these defeats to come now, rather than in a major tournament.

Speaking to Sky Sport (via MilanNews) after the game at San Siro, Rabiot praised the opposition goalkeeper – a remark made after an incredible save against him – as well as looking at where France stand after a few games under Zidane.

A leader of Milan and France. How much does this defeat weigh on the standings?

“It will be a tough game to play, the last one, because we need to win. The coach told us it’s part of the journey. We’re on a new path and we’re doing some things well, others a little less so. Tonight was a great game to watch.

“We did some very good things, but not so much in the second half. They showed a little more determination and deserved to win.”

“Donnarumma did well. We could have closed the game out in the first half because we were in a better position than them. In the second half, it was the opposite, even though he made two or three incredible saves. That’s part of football. They played a good game. They have strong, new players.

“It’s not easy, but I wish them the best because there’s a lot to do. It was an exciting match.”

#1660. Trinidad and Tobago vs Antigua and Barbuda - prediction, team news, lineups

By Saikat Mandal | 14 Nov 2026 14:55, Last updated: 14 Nov 2026 16:09

Trinidad and Tobago will host Antigua and Barbuda at the Hasely Crawford Stadium on Tuesday for the second leg of their CONCACAF Nations League tie, with a place in the 2027 CONCACAF Gold Cup Prelims at stake.

The home side head into the encounter with a slender advantage after claiming a 3-2 victory in the first leg of the Play-In tie, and will need another strong performance to secure their place in the next stage of Gold Cup qualification.

It has been a dismal campaign so far for Trinidad and Tobago, who are yet to register a victory in the CONCACAF Nations League, League A.

The Soca Warriors sit fifth in the relegation zone with just one point from four matches, although they have managed to avoid defeat in their last two outings.

After suffering three consecutive losses, Derek King's side secured a 1-1 draw against Curacao before claiming victory over Antigua and Barbuda in their most recent match.

Their defensive record remains a major concern, having failed to keep a clean sheet in their last 14 matches, but the latest win over Antigua marked their 13th victory in 16 meetings between the two nations.

Antigua and Barbuda made a dream start in the first leg, taking an early lead through an own goal from Ryan Telfer.

However, the visitors fought their way back into the contest and scored three quick goals to establish a 3-1 advantage at half time, before Brandon Satchell's stoppage-time strike gave Jacques Passy's side renewed hope ahead of the return fixture.

The Benna Boys have enjoyed an impressive League C campaign, finishing top of Group B with nine points from four matches.

They have also scored 13 goals in their last four outings and, despite their first-leg defeat, can take confidence from their attacking form as they look to find the net again and make life difficult for Trinidad and Tobago on Tuesday.

Trinidad and Tobago CONCACAF Nations League form:

Antigua and Barbuda CONCACAF Nations League form:

Molik Khan was outstanding for Trinidad and Tobago in the first leg and is likely to retain his place in the starting lineup, although Nathaniel James could provide an alternative.

Tyrese Spicer and Dante Sealy remain unavailable through injury, but Daniel David and Kaihim Thomas could be handed more playing time.

Kylano Issac and Leroy Graham struggled to make an impact in the previous game for Antigua and Barbuda, but both are still expected to retain their places in a 4-3-3 formation.

#1658. Gibraltar vs Malta - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matthew Cooper | 14 Nov 2026 15:17, Last updated: 14 Nov 2026 16:14

Gibraltar will be looking to finish their UEFA Nations League campaign on a positive note when they welcome Malta to Europa Point Stadium on Monday evening.

The visitors have already secured top spot in their League D group, while the hosts will be keen to pick up their first win.

Gibraltar have picked up just two Nations League points so far, with two draws and one defeat from three games.

Scott Wiseman's side began their campaign with a goalless draw against Andorra, but they earned a respectable 1-1 stalemate away to Malta four days later, with James Scanlon scoring the equaliser.

However, Friday's 2-0 defeat away to Andorra was a disappointing result, with Guillaume Lopez and Albert Rosas Ubach on target for the hosts.

Although a victory over Malta on Monday would see Gibraltar leapfrog Andorra into second, there is a real lack of jeopardy surrounding the fixture.

Due to a restructuring of the Nations League, every side in League D will be promoted to League C for the 2028-29 edition.

Malta, meanwhile, have enjoyed an impressive Nations League campaign and would have been promoted to League C anyway under the original rules.

Emilio De Leo's side are unbeaten and have collected seven points from their three group games so far.

Malta have picked up two victories over Andorra, beating them 2-1 and 1-0, and also drawing 1-1 with Malta.

In their most recent game, Malta were held to a 1-1 stalemate in a friendly against Eswatini, who were down to 10 men for much of the game after Gift Gamedze was sent off.

Malta will be keen to get back to winning ways on Monday and De Leo is expected to name a much stronger side, having rotated on Thursday.

Gibraltar will need at least one change after Friday's loss to Andorra, with Tjay De Barr suspended after picking up another booking.

Ethan Jolley is also a doubt after he was forced off with an injury in the 33rd minute against Andorra, with Louie Annesley expected to replace him.

Malta, meanwhile, will be without Alexander Satariano, who is suspended for the final group fixture after receiving a one-match ban.

The likes of Teddy Teuma, Ilyas Chouaref and Brandon Paiber could all come into the side, while Basil Tuma is set to be rewarded with a start after scoring off the bench against Eswatini.

Hankins; Annesley, Bent, Lopes, Valarino; Pozo, Ronan; Richards, Scanlon, Mason; Borge

Bonello; Lonardelli, Muscat, Shaw, Beerman; Guillaumier, Paiber; Mbong, Teuma, Chouaref; Tuma

Gibraltar should provide a tough test for Malta, but the visitors are unbeaten in the Nations League for a reason and should have enough quality to pick up the win.

#1656. Opinion: Liverpool will sign their next Fabinho if they make move for €50m midfielder

Fabinho left Liverpool in 2023 and they still haven't properly replaced him.

When the Brazilian was initially brought in, his transfer was a complete surprise.

It felt like fans had just woken up one day and, all of a sudden, they had a new defensive midfielder in town.

The five years that the midfielder spent at Anfield were excellent. He won every trophy possible and was a key cog in Jurgen Klopp's system.

However, after his form dropped off, the Reds were quick to move him on with many fans believing that this was because they'd have a replacement lined up.

Evidently, that wasn't the case as, even though Fabinho was sold in July 2023, Liverpool still haven't replaced him, but, that could all be about to change.

Angelo Stiller is ready to leave VFB Stuttgart as soon as possible

Defensive midfield has been a major issue for Liverpool over the last couple of years.

No matter who the Reds try and use there, things just don't quite work out.

Recently, Alexis Mac Allister and Trey Nyoni have been Andoni Iraola's preferred options but, since Mac Allister isn't a natural number six and Nyoni is still only 19 years old, neither of them are the best possible options for Liverpool to have.

So, that's why this latest update from Florian Plettenberg is something that could excite the Reds' fanbase.

"Angelo Stiller and his agency, Sports360, have parted ways by mutual consent. However, the initiative came from the agency, with differing views on the player’s future," he shared via X.

"Stiller is once again very open to a move. Saudi Arabia, MLS and Türkiye are also options. Contract with VfB Stuttgart valid until 2028."

Angelo Stiller could become Liverpool's next Fabinho

A completely natural number six is a rare thing to find in football these days.

Most defensive midfielders try their best to cover every single aspect of being a midfielder and, in the end, none of them end up with a specialised position.

But, with how attacking Iraola's tactics are, Liverpool are a team who need a natural number six that can defend and help keep their back line solid.

Angelo Stiller has been on the Reds' radar for some time now with the Reds and Real Madrid both being linked in the past.

A fee worth around €50 million (£41.7 million) is what would be required to prise him from the Bundesliga outfit which, with how good he is, feels like an absolute steal.

The German has played in 328 games across his career so far despite only being 25 years old.

This experience coupled with his defensive capability are the two reasons why Stiller could be the Reds' new Fabinho.

Obviously, the fact that interest in the midfielder has died down recently also plays in Liverpool's favour and could mean that they get a few more million knocked off the deal which would be even better. Here's hoping that a deal is struck soon.

Or that Liverpool at least re-ignite their interest in signing him.

#1655. Liverpool 0-1 Arsenal: Resolute Gunners dig in for a big Anfield win

Fourteen years is a long time to wait for a win at any stadium, but Arsenal ensured all three points returned from Anfield to North London for the first time since 2012 yesterday.

The surprise in the team line-up was the return of Christos Tzolis who had missed a month, more or less, with a hamstring injury. If it initially felt a bit harsh on Eberechi Eze, Mikel Arteta’s post-game comments about him barely making the game because of an injury problem of his own made it make more sense.

Early on, we were really good. Plenty of the ball, playing it well in their half, and lots of control. Liverpool looked a bit off the pace, and in the opening minutes young midfielder Trey Nyoni was lucky to escape without some sanction for a nasty foul on Martin Odegaard. I think it was much more mistimed than malicious, but studs down the Achilles is never good, and we saw Crystal Palace striker Jean Philippe Mateta see red for something similar on Saturday evening.

The early pressure paid dividends when Liverpool were a little sloppy at the back. Odegaard pounced to recover the ball, it was fed to Noni Madueke via Bruno Guimaraes, and when Declan Rice overlapped, his precision ball to the back post found Kai Havertz for a tap-in to make it 1-0. That makes it 5 assists so far this season for the midfielder, all of them from open play as well, and his presence in this team reminds me so much of Patrick Vieira. Not that they’re the same kind of player, but that his importance and stature is just fundamental to us. The desire he showed with that overlap is, essentially, what cracked this game open in our favour.

There was another back post chance for Havertz, almost getting on the end of a deflected Guimaraes shot, but after that – as happens so often at Anfield – the momentum changed. This time there was no Granit Xhaka style confrontation to act as a catalyst, the game just shifted and in the final 20 minutes of the first half we rode our luck a bit.

Liverpool started to play around our box and deliver dangerous balls. One almost found Alexander Isak but a combination of David Raya and Ezri Konsa was enough to see it trickle wide. Florian Wirtz hit the bar with a free kick, and Liverpool wanted a penalty when Tzolis looked to pull back Cody Gakpo but I don’t think there was enough in that one. The next one, however, oooof.

Liverpool put in another dangerous cross, Isak was there to head towards goal from close range, and Jurrien Timber’s shirt pull absolutely prevented him from making contact with the ball. You know my rule of thumb with penalties: how would I feel it were given, or not given, up the other end, and if we didn’t get that I’d be fuming. It’s a penalty all day long, and even if the ref didn’t quite see the foul well enough, the VAR officials really ought to have suggested an on-field review. I found the focus on Isak’s reaction a bit odd. Surely the onus is on the officials to recognise what we’ve all seen without a player having to prompt them in that direction, but we got so, so lucky there.

As we did when Alexis Mac Allister ran into the box and, unmarked from 10 yards out, headed the ball over the bar when he absolutely should score. That was a very bad miss from a Liverpool perspective, and a huge chance to equalise just before the break. We needed half-time, and despite the fact Liverpool enjoyed plenty of the ball in the early part of the second period, they looked a lot less dangerous.

My explanation for this is that we leaned into one of our great strengths, which is our defensive organisation and discipline. I thought Konsa was outstanding, but so too was Riccardo Calafiori at left-back whose one on one defending has improved massively. He dealt with Gakpo, he then had to contend with Rio Ngumoha, and I just loved the concentration as he focused on the ball and more often than not prevented Liverpool from creating danger.

Myles Lewis-Skelly came on midfield, Odegaard’s pressing was relentless, and as I remarked on BlueSky afterwards, if this team could attack half as well as it can defend, we’d be the best team in the world by a mile. There were moments when we could have countered better and with more pace, but we still found some threat in the second 45. The best chance fell to Tzolis, set up by Madueke, and his first-time shot was heading for the bottom corner but for a brilliant save from Alisson.

Liverpool threw the kitchen sink at it from the bench, but it made little difference. Mac Allister then got a bit naughty, slapping Odegaard on the back of the head, then collapsing to the ground to make it look as if Madueke had leaned his head into him. Replays showed that didn’t happen, and it was pretty pathetic from the Argentina international. I guess, as well as being a risible piece of play-acting, there was an element of desperation to it, because Liverpool huffed and puffed but could not blow our house down because of how defensively outstanding we are as a team.

For the first time in Premier League history, Liverpool finished a home game without a shot on target, which tells you something. It probably tells you just how much that Timber shirt pull had an impact because a striker like Isak would at least have tested David Raya from there, but more broadly it tells you that this is a team who look laser-focused on their target this season which is to retain the title – something we’ve never done in the modern era.

Afterwards, I thought the manager’s turn of phrase was interesting when he referred to it as ‘a mission’, saying:

Just loving the mission and the mission was something that we didn’t accomplish in 14 years. You really need to enjoy that. If you don’t, there will be a moment that you will switch off and they will punish you. I think the way we competed and played and the chances that we generated as well, it was really impressive so I’m really happy.

He’s obviously referencing winning away at Liverpool for the first time in such a long time, but I think it applies to the season as well. And, as I referenced in yesterday’s blog, there was a response to the midweek defeat to Fleetwood Town. If that was a result that as fans we could find relatively easy to compartmentalise, I don’t think the same is true for this manager because we know he wants to win every game, and it how much it stings when we don’t – especially against lower league opposition. He expected his side to deliver, saying:

It was a feeling, how the hell can that happen? How can you get out of the cup when you shoot 27 times? We had the chances that we had against a team that had put one shot on target and then you look so silly. Then you have to go to Anfield and say, how can I lift those players up? I had a feeling and I said, now is the moment. We’re going to have to dig deep, have an element of luck at times and for sure a lot of quality in the key moments and we’ve done it.

Which I think is a pretty fair assessment. We did a lot of stuff very well, we had moments of luck – which you so often need in a game like this to take all three points – but I don’t think anyone should be under any illusions that this was anything other than the champions demonstrating our title credentials again. In every season, regardless of how good you are, you need the rub of the green from time to time, like a Ruud van Nistelrooy penalty miss at Old Trafford, or Mateus Fernandes missing a huge chance for West Ham. It doesn’t change the inherent quality you possess or what you’re capable of doing, and in the cold light of day it should make you more driven to ensure you widen the margins – and by that I mean delivering a bit more in the opposition’s final third.

However, no complaints this morning. We had a job to do, and a difficult one at that, and we did exactly that to put us back on top of the table. It’s a nice place to be, but it’s still so early in the season I think we should dismiss any chat about what it means at this point. We can be impressed, but still cognisant of the fact there’s still a long, long way to go.

Right, I’ll leave it there for now, but we will have an Arsecast Extra for you a bit later on today. We’ve already put out the call for questions on BlueSky @gunnerblog.bsky.social and @arseblog.com, so fire away using the hashtag #arsecastextra – or if you’re an Arseblog Member on Patreon, leave your question in the #arsecast-extra-questions channel on our Discord server.

The pod should be out around around noon or so. Until then, have a good one.

#1654. Next USA manager: Gareth Southgate one of four 'candidates' to replace Mauricio Pochettino

By Darren Plant | 14 Nov 2026 16:06

The United States Soccer Federation may reportedly approach Gareth Southgate to become their next manager.

Earlier this week, it was confirmed that Mauricio Pochettino will become the new Manchester United boss after the CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final against Haiti.

With Pochettino taking charge of the next two games, it gives US soccer chiefs time to find a permanent successor for their next meaningful fixtures in March.

A report has suggested that former Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola has been identified as a potential candidate.

According to TEAMtalk, there are three other names that have been highlighted behind the scenes, including Southgate's.

The report emphasises that trying to tempt Guardiola to take the job is the priority of US soccer chiefs.

Nevertheless, Southgate, ex-Portugal boss Roberto Martinez and former Newcastle United manager Eddie Howe are also viewed as possible successors.

In the case of Southgate, he has not been in the dugout since guiding England to the Euro 2024 final, where they lost to Spain.

Southgate has previously hinted that he may not manage another team, and the report suggests that there is currently little chance that he would consider becoming the new USA boss.

Furthermore, it is suggested that the 56-year-old is more likely to take a role at the Football Association than take another managerial job.

In December, a USA squad that will largely include MLS-based players will face Jamaica in a friendly, but the presence of that game on the schedule will not speed up the process to appoint a new manager.

Instead, discussions with suitable candidates are likely to take a number of weeks, with the onus on Pochettino's replacement being prepared for games scheduled for March.

The only way that the process will speed up is through Guardiola accepting any approach for his services.

Liverpool want to return to the pinnacle of football, and for that they need the best players on the planet.

Ifeanyi Ndukwe already looks like an incredible value for money. Mor Talla Ndiaye could prove to be the same. Daniele De Rossi has looked back at Genoa’s defeat to AC Milan and how he wasn’t frustrated with his team afterwards.

Milan entered the international break with a much-needed victory against Genoa, but it wasn’t the easiest result of the season. We indeed lost against Milan, but we lost ‘well.’ We didn’t deserve it. Three or four weeks ago, the latest results seemed like a pipe dream. I thank the players, staff, and my club for giving me faith and patience at a time when other clubs wouldn’t have had it.

“They remembered how good we did last year. I’m happy to have emerged from a difficult period and to be Genoa’s coach; I’m really happy there.”

“I’m passionate about the fans and the supporters. I’m part of a club that, in terms of fan base, is among the best in Europe. I’m passionate; I don’t punch a clock. I spend two hours with the stockman or the waitress with the same enthusiasm I spend time with the team captain. Experiencing it like that, you realise that Genoa is a great team.

“Genoa is full of Genoese fans who remind you every second how much they love their club, the pride of being the top club in Italy. The architecture of the stadium and the warmth of the fans… I’m not saying this to be a sycophant, but on Sunday Moreira came to me and said, ‘I’ve never seen anything like this here in Italy.’ It’s a reality that even our opponents notice.”

#1650. Fridges and pigs and scoring goals

We live in strange times. Sorry to start your day with this shocking revelation, I realise this is a bit of a bolt from the blue, but it’s fact. All across Europe supermarket fridges are being hacked. What a time to be alive. They used to hack, I dunno, mainframes and banks and shit, but now they’re hacking fridges.

Maybe they just got bored taking billions of made-up money from CryptoSloth and BitWomble and needed a challenge. I feel like fridges ought to be the kind of thing you just can’t hack – beyond unplugging it – but what do I know? Anyway, it’s an example of how the inter-connectivity that brings us all together every day is being weaponised and now the sliced meats in your local store are gone off because Neo pwned some large cold cupboards. As if we don’t have enough to deal with.

Such as all the people who hate the way Arsenal play. Let me be very clear, my days of caring what other people think about this football club, or pretty much anything else that’s important to me, are gone. It’s a waste of time. It’s a bit like quote that’s often attributed to George Bernard Shaw, which says ‘Never wrestle with pigs. You both get dirty and the pig likes it.’

I don’t think he actually said that, but I think we can all connect with the meaning. It applies so much to social media, and to many of the ways we’re exposed to punditry and ‘expert’ analysis in football these days. Like one of those shows where you have a couple of ex-pro pigs bleating on about this and that, and then a collection of other little pigs who support all the clubs argue with them and amongst themselves, and it’s just a pigstravaganza of pointless, inane bollocks but it does #numbers on socials so is seen as valuable #content.

I understand why opposition fans go on and on about how much they hate how Arsenal play. It’s because we win a lot of games. That’s the thing that really irks them. That’s just so basic though, you can’t appear to be clever and an aficionado of the game if you just say ‘I don’t like it when they win’, so it’s dressed up as dismissal of style or something else.

And look, here’s where the strange world we live in comes back into focus. You can, and really should, be able to hold more than one thought in your brain – about football or anything else – that holds true. I absolutely love how good we are defensively. LOVE IT. The commitment with which we are determined not to give the opposition anything is truly something to relish. Players laser-focused on their one on ones; putting bodies on the line to block shots and crosses; 11 players moving like a murmuration of birds because they’re so well drilled and organised; off the awareness and discipline; brilliantly timed tackles and headers and clearances; lads sticking up for each other when the opposition get a bit snide, as we saw on Sunday with Jurrien Timber and Noni Madueke refusing to allow their captain to be treated that way; it’s all part of a brilliantly defiant defensive attitude that runs right through this team.

Creating that is not easy. As Arsenal fans we have endured defences that were porous and feeble and, at times, very, very stupid. I do not long for a return to those times. Over the years Mikel Arteta has assembled a collection of players who cannot wait to go out there and do the dirty work of defending, and it runs from front to back because that’s what he demands. If it was that easy, everyone would do it, so to castigate a team’s brilliance in one department because you just lost to them without a shot on target just comes across as sour grapes.

Here’s the other thought though. I’d really like us to be a bit better from an attacking perspective, and when I look at this team and what it’s capable of, there’s no question the forward line remains the area where you can see the room for improvement. We defend as well as we do because, more often than you or I might like, we have to – because we live through games of fine margins. A 1-0 to the Arsenal is part of our history, hard-wired into our supporter DNA (particularly if you’re of a particular vintage), but I can’t lie and wish there weren’t a few more 3-0s to the Arsenal.

I’m absolutely certain Mikel Arteta would like that too, and I think it’s a bit too easy to say that this is a team that plays precisely the football he wants it to play. He is, as we all understand, an arch pragmatist, so what we get is a team that leans into its strengths, as laid out above. He is characterised as a defensive coach, which I get, but a few seasons ago we found an attacking cocktail that drove a title challenge, and saw us score more goals that year than the Invincibles did when they won the league in 2004 (91 to 73).

I think he wants both. He wants that parsimony at the back and the firepower up front. Unfortunately, forward line recruitment is the most difficult part of transfer business, and while he as manager has a part to play in that, as a club our track record is quite poor in that regard. This summer’s window was a complete bust from an attacking perspective, not a good look when you’re pursuing players like Morgan Rogers, Vinicius Junior and Julian Alvarez. When you then let three forwards go and add just one, there are questions to be asked of the people in charge. Arteta among them, of course, but he’s not the one whose job it is to get the deals done.

It’s why there are so many conversations around January, and what we might do. We see other clubs recruit forwards who produce on a consistent basis, while ours too often struggle to find that end product. Is it our system? Would these players find it hard to get those goals for us? Reasonable questions, but the bottom line in my opinion is that we have A+ options at the back and in midfield, while in that front three we’re a bit C-. That’s where the room for improvement is, that’s where the recruitment needs to be better (certainly better than no recruitment at all), and that’s how the games we currently win by a single goal margin, often by virtue of our defensive strength, become a bit more routine.

Simplistic? Yes. Easier said than done? Quite probably. But necessary? Absolutely. Until then though, expect more defensive masterclasses, more pig wrestling, and perhaps someone could hack our own Swedish fridge into scoring a few more goals. Worth a try!

Right, I’ll leave it there for now. I just have a small favour to ask. Arseblog has been nominated for Best Fan Media (Fran Merida) in the 2026 FSA Awards. #1649. How Nico Paz compares to Bruno Fernandes as Man United consider Como star amid captain's contract uncertainty

By Ellis Stevens | 14 Nov 2026 17:04, Last updated: 14 Nov 2026 17:14

The mood surrounding Manchester United is already one of misery given their disastrous start to the 2026-27 Premier League season, with the Red Devils sitting inside the relegation zone with just eight points after 10 matches.

Cautious optimism may have started to return following the announcement of Mauricio Pochettino as the new Manchester United manager, but the Red Devils have already been dealt another potential blow in the early days of the new boss' tenure.

Reports have emerged that captain Bruno Fernandes has rejected a second offer of a new deal at Old Trafford, leaving his long-term future uncertain as his current contract approaches its expiry in June 2027 - although the Red Devils do have the option to extend his stay by a further 12 months.

As the Portugal international is yet to commit his future to the club, subsequent reports have suggested that Man Utd are monitoring Nico Paz as a potential replacement in the summer transfer window.

Securing Paz's signature would certainly not be straightforward, with Real Madrid retaining a buy-back clause and several of Europe's elite sides likely to join the race, but replacing Fernandes and becoming Man Utd's new talisman under fellow Argentine Pochettino could prove tempting.

With speculation continuing to circulate around Fernandes' future and Manchester United's reported interest in Paz, Sports Mole takes a closer look at how the two players compare.

Although both Fernandes and Paz operate in the traditional number 10 position, the two players bring a very different style and ability in possession.

In 2026-27, and throughout his more recent years at Old Trafford, Fernandes has thrived as Manchester United's primary creative operator, with almost every attack flowing through the Portugal international.

As demonstrated by his Premier League record-breaking 21 assists last season, as well as creating 0.44 big chances per 90 in the league this term, Fernandes' greatest strength is his ability to pick out dangerous passes.

In comparison, Paz, while capable of picking out a threaded pass - as shown with 0.22 through balls per 90 in Serie A this season - is at his best when carrying the ball.

Paz attempts a considerable 3.50 dribbles per 90 in Serie A, completing 1.97 of them, whereas Fernandes averages just 0.89 attempted dribbles and 0.22 successful dribbles per 90 minutes.

While Paz is able to then create an opportunity for a teammate, with 0.22 big chances created per 90, the Argentine often prefers to manoeuvre himself into goalscoring positions.

Paz has taken 5.03 shots per 90 minutes in the Serie A, scoring 0.33 goals per 90, while Fernandes has taken 3.44 shots per 90. Although the Portugal international has scored at a greater frequency, with 0.44 goals per 90, two of his four goals have come from the penalty spot, while Paz's strikes have all come from open play.

Paz's ability to play in a possession-oriented side must also be taken into consideration, with the Argentine playing a key role in Cesc Fabregas's Como, who boast the highest average possession in Serie A this season (61.6%).

Fernandes, while one of the best in European football at consistently creating chances, has a track record for seemingly preferring to attempt ambitious passes rather than recycling the ball.

While that is undoubtedly what makes Fernandes such a phenomenal chance creator, forcing the midfielder into a system that operates around keeping the ball more often may subtract from arguably his greatest quality.

As a result of his tendency to look for the most dangerous pass, Fernandes' successful pass percentage stands at 80.9% this season, compared to Paz's considerably higher 87.94% pass completion.

Given Pochettino's recent tendency to create teams with a possession-based identity, demonstrated by his Chelsea side boasting around 59% average possession - which would place them in the top four of Premier League teams this term - Paz may better suit the new Manchester United's identity.

However, it must be noted that Paz, due to his more adventurous dribbling approach, is dispossessed 0.87 times per 90 this season, compared to Fernandes' figure of 0.78.

While both certainly bring their respective strengths in possession, shown by their attacking numbers, their defensive and off-ball contributions are equally as important.

Paz's numbers show that the 22-year-old could offer a greater physical presence in midfield, particularly when competing for possession and challenging opponents in individual duels.

The Como midfielder averages 11.7 duels per 90 minutes, almost double Fernandes' figure of 6.00, while Paz also wins considerably more of those contests, recording 6.89 successful duels compared to the Portugal international's 2.11.

Paz's physical advantage is also evident in aerial situations, with the Argentina international's 6'1" frame helping him to win 0.87 aerial duels per 90 minutes, while Fernandes, standing at 5'10", wins just 0.11 of his aerial contests.

Fernandes does cover more ground, covering 101.3km in nine league matches to Paz's 88.4km covered in 10 league games.

However, Fernandes is often used as Manchester United's trigger for the press, although the Red Devils captain can also be seen charging forward without support on numerous occasions throughout matches.

Paz's ability both in and out of possession were witnessed first-hand by Manchester United in their 4-1 defeat to Como in the Champions League earlier this season.

Nico Paz capitalises on a mistake from Carlos Baleba to extend Como's lead against Manchester United to 3-0 ? He's been involved in each goal ? ? Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/D7kD8PGtcY

The Argentine dispossessed Carlos Baleba before driving nearly 25 metres up the pitch and converting pass Senne Lammens to make it 3-1 - marking his second goal of the game after also netting a stunning strike from just inside the box in the second minute.

Paz also registered the assist for Anastasios Douvikas's goal in that victory, and that impressive performance is surely one of several reasons why the Red Devils hold an interest in the attacking midfielder.

#1648. Xabi Alonso hits out at ‘soft’ Chelsea players

Xabi Alonso accused his Chelsea players of being “soft” after they failed to keep a clean sheet for the 20th successive Premier League game.

Chelsea threw away an early lead to draw 2-2 with Hull City and have conceded two or more goals in each of their four Premier League games.

Alonso has tried different systems and different players in those games, but suggested Chelsea’s biggest problem is mental.

The club’s dreadful clean-sheet record pre-dates him and is the first time in 65 years Chelsea have gone 20 league games without keeping the opposition out.

Hull’s first goal from Mohamed Belloumi came after the ball had bounced over Jorrel Hato and Alonso said: “We need to be aware that from any situation, any team in the Premier League can hurt you. Today it was from a long ball, two bounces, the way it happened. You need to be very aware, very ready that the danger can come from any situation. If you are soft or if you are not prepared, you will get punished and we have been punished that way.”

Chelsea have shared 30 goals with their opponents in the club’s six games in all competitions so far this season.

“Yeah, it’s all maybe entertaining, but I hope that one day you say it was a boring game and we win and we don’t give these entertaining moments,” he said.

“But, for sure, it kind of repeats some patterns that we are making. It will take time to... or it will take moments to fix them when we get the lead and you still need to be competing and not give the chance so easily for them to come back, especially in the first goal, we can do much better.

“It was too soft to give them this hope because until then we were controlling, we were creating chances. But that momentum that we had changed the mood and the score of the game, and it’s something that we need to be talking [about], we address and we will get better. But it’s having an impact on our performances at the moment.”

Asked if his players have a real desire to defend and keep clean sheets, Alonso said: “We can do better, we can do better for sure. We need to know that even when we have the lead, a very important part of the game is to hold together, to keep the distance, to go intense in the situations to defend. I’m sure that we can do better.

“Overall, I think that we are attacking better than defending in every part. We know that it’s a big topic and a big theme for us. For sure, it’s just four games. But the dynamic in terms of conceding, I don’t like it and we need to do much better. Open play, set-pieces, long balls, this toughness, this competitive sense, we can do better.”

Needing three goals or more to win games is not sustainable, as Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso is finding out.

This is not a problem of Alonso’s making, given Chelsea have now gone 20 Premier League games without a clean sheet. But he is certainly not improving the issue yet.

Chelsea beat Fulham with three goals and Brighton with four but left themselves far too much to do against Arsenal and were taken advantage of by Hull City, who will be slightly disappointed they did not leave Stamford Bridge with all three points.

Goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez has now conceded seven goals in three games since joining from Aston Villa, while central defender Maxence Lacroix, who joined for £52m from Crystal Palace in the summer, was relegated to the substitutes’ bench.

Martínez was at fault for Mohamed Belloumi’s second goal, but the Argentine did make a crucial save at his back post to stop substitute Mohamed-Ali Cho grabbing a winner that Chelsea could have had no complaints about.

Hull finished the game with more shots on goal than their hosts and a higher expected-goals rate. Chelsea are far too open and in some ways far too entertaining.

Defensive midfielder Moisés Caicedo cannot return from injury quickly enough, but this does not feel like a problem that will be solved by one man. Alonso needs to find a balance and instil a real desire in his team to defend.

Caicedo has that desire, but there are no defenders at the club who have shown that absolute desperation to keep the ball out of the net that Chelsea fans became so used to in the days of John Terry, Gary Cahill and César Azpilicueta.

None of this should diminish Hull’s performance. They were not only spirited and full of character but also showed quality and a threat. The joke is currently on those who laughed at their hopes of survival before a ball had been kicked.

It is now two wins and two draws for Sergej Jakirovic’s team and they are already a fifth of the way to 40 points. Jakirovic had promised his staff a week off in the international break if they reached eight points after five games. With that target already met, there may be a new reward if Hull can make it 11 points against Newcastle United next weekend.

“Before the season, I said to my staff that we will take seven, eight points in these first five and then I will give them seven days off,” Jakirovic said. “That was our target and now we are in a very good position, eight points.

“Especially today, it’s very, very difficult to play here, and now we will try to get even more. Of course, I’m a little bit worried about the international break because we have 13 national team players. But we will see who will come back and in what condition. So this is my concern right now.” Asked if his staff’s seven-day break will be extended if Hull can beat Newcastle, Jakirovic added: “I will tell them. But I know already.”

While his five-game target may need modifying, Jakirovic is not deviating from his goal for the season for Hull. “Our target is always to stay in the league and collect as many points as possible,” he said. “Forty points, 38 to 41, this is the average we need. Then it’s easier to play. You can play more relaxed, with more joy and happiness. So [get to] this as soon as possible, so that we are safe.”

Hull had not conceded a league goal before this and there had been predictions they might crumble when they finally let the ball into their net. They did so after just seven minutes but they kept their heads and came back stronger.

It was far too easy for Morgan Rogers to make a yard of space for himself to shoot after collecting the ball from João Pedro, and Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis may not have been happy to have been beaten at his near post.

Chelsea have now scored inside the first 10 minutes in all of their four league games, but Hull were in no mood to crumble and hit back with two goals in six minutes from Belloumi to take a half-time lead. Both Hull goals were shockers from Chelsea’s perspective. The first, in the 28th minute, came as a result of Jorrel Hato letting the ball bounce over him from a Ryan Giles cross and Belloumi finished brilliantly.

Belloumi’s second came after Martínez had flapped at a corner and Semi Ajayi had hit the bar with a header. The ball fell to Belloumi again and his shot was deflected into the net.

It was no surprise that Hato did not reappear for the second half, as he was replaced by Pep Chavarría at left-back. But Chelsea remained vulnerable and Martínez had to recover from spilling a Regan Slater shot to prevent Ollie McBurnie extending Hull’s advantage.

When Palmer and Pedro combined for Pedro to sweep the ball into the net and equalise with 24 minutes remaining, it seemed like it would be Chelsea who would provide the grandstand finish.

But it was Hull who got a second wind and Chelsea were indebted to Martínez for making a save to stop Cho securing all three points and sending the visiting fans home even happier.

I feel good. We have to be happy. It’s a huge result for us.

We had 2-1 at half-time and we had a 100 per cent chance with McBurnie but Martinez’s save was excellent. We have to control play better in the box because we can stop this [Chelsea goal]. We had an excellent chance for Cho – Martinez saved again. Player of the match.

We can be very happy. We took a point in a very demanding match.

Eight points against very difficult opponents. We have to continue like this.

There have been 12 Premier League games at Anfield in 2026, Liverpool have only won 4 of them to date. This was seventh draw and Fulham deserves their share of the spoils. This was very much a learning experience for Andoni Iraola.

Not a single home win in the Premier League, today.

Aston Villa 1 Nottingham Forest 2Bournemouth 2 Brentford 2Chelsea 2 Hull City 2Crystal Palace 2 Ipswich Town 3Liverpool 0 Fulham 0

What a result for Hull, who remain unbeaten and they have taken five points from fixtures against United, Villa and Chelsea.

That is the first really poor result of the Alonso era, points dropped.

What a thriller in SE25, both teams have been going for it in the closing stages, but Ipswich have surely score the winner through Zian Flemming.

Fulham were pointless before this game, but they have kept a clean sheet at Anfield with a disciplined display and they could well have score one or two. Underwhelming for Liverpool, who have not won just one of their first four games and their fixtures have not been the most taxing.

And as we predicted at the beginning of the game... Liverpool 0 Fulham 0. If this reporter ever gives you advice on a horse to back or a team to follow, make sure you take the opposite stance. Fulham deserve their reward and their fans are singing “We got a point!”

Villa are finishing the game with 10 men because Ian Maatsen pulled up after Emery had made his five substitutions, and Forest have punished them through Igor Jesus with just a few minutes of normal time to play.

Alexander Isak heads over the bar when he perhaps should have hit the target. Has time run out for Liverpool?

You might imagine Chelsea are battering down the door, but Mohamed-Ali Cho has just forced Emi Martinez into a save at the other end. Hull will remain unbeaten if they can hold out.

Strand Larsen has had his critics, but he has scored his first goal of the season to set up a grandstand finish with 15 minutes plus stoppage time to play at Selhurst Park.

Short corner, McGinn whipped in an inswinging cross that is glanced into the bottom corner by Alysson.

Liverpool continue to toil at Anfield, but no opening goal. Iraola has thrown on Frimpong, Mac Allister, Ngumoha and Gakpo in the second half. Fulham have had the chances to score at least one, and Josh King has just brought a save out of Alisson.

Hull are a little lucky they still have 11 men on the pitch. Already on a booking, my man Crooks bundled down Rogers. It could easily have been another yellow car but the referee let him off and now he’s been replaced by Iroegbunam.

Joao Pedro finds the smallest of gaps to be the goalkeeper and find the roof of the net with a brilliant, instinctive finish.

That had not really been coming for Chelsea. It all felt a bit easy for Palmer to get his low cross into the box and Pedro to sweep the ball in. The home fans have woken up again.

Martinez was lucky to get away with another slip up, there. He spilt Slater’s shot but reacted before McBurnie to stop the Hull striker scoring the rebound. Just a day after his nasty looking crash, Sorba Thomas is on for Hull.

This game is absolutely here for Fulham to win. Quietness has descended around Anfield, the hosts have no fluency in their play and Fulham are growing in confidence. Why wouldn’t they after getting to 65 minutes with a clean sheet?

Just like in the first half, four minutes after one of these teams taking the lead there has been an equaliser. Kevin Scahde is in a rich vein of form.

Bournemouth have have never beaten Brentford in the Premier League, but they might well be on their way to changing that record having trailed earlier in the game. Marcus Tavernier has just scored their second goal.

Matt Davidson Rider Crooks has just been booked for a very cynical foul on Rogers. It gave Chelsea a free-kick in a dangerous position Reece James had an effort tipped away. Chelsea have started the second half well

Within a minute of the restart, Villa lose the ball in midfield and Delap punishes them to the maximum. Cracking finish from just outside the box, and a much-needed goal by Delap. The Glasner curse striking for Emery again?

Liam Delap has just started paying back that £50m transfer fee with a fine goal.

Delap picked the ball up on the left and set himself up on the edge of the box before crashing a 25-yard shot past Zion Suzuki.

Unai Emery has made a couple of changes at half-time, taking off Nicolas Jackson who picked up a silly booking just before half-time.

Tammy Abraham is on in his place. George Hemmings is also off and replaced by Alysson.

Pep Chavarria on for Chelsea at half-time. He’s replaced Jorrel Hato, who had a bit of a stinker in the first half.

Andoni Iraola hasn’t hung about here. Milos Kerkez has come on immediately after half-time for Kostas Tsimikas and you can say with certainty that Liverpool will be shopping for a new left-back in due course.

So at half-time, Hull City are top of the Premier League and don’t their supporters know it? They were singing “we are top of the League” for the full two minutes of time added on for stoppages at the end of the first period. Alonso has some work to do at the break.

Forest did need a brilliant double save from Matz Sels to deny Victor Lindelof and have recovered to slow the match down.

Neco Williams wasted a decent chance for Forest from outside the penalty area shortly before the break.

Referee Andrew Madley has irritated both teams with a number of weird decisions - but that’s sadly par for the course with officials nowadays.

Villa 0 Forest 0Bournemouth 1 Brentford 1Chelsea 1 Hull City 2Palace 1 Ipswich 2Liverpool 0 Fulham 0

Palace in some trouble now, level with Ipswich and down to 10 men. Disasi was sent off in the 34th minute for a reckless challenge on Jack Clarke, caught him with studs on shin.

Things got worse for Palace just before half-time, with Leif Davis heading home at the back post to give Ipswich the league.

Apologies for the lack of updates, some technical gremlins at Telegraph Towers. A nip and tuck game as expected at at the Vitality: Kevin Schade gave Brentford the lead before Justin Kluivert equalised four minutes later.

One way to put it is that Kostas Tsimikas isn’t playing well. Another way to say it would be that his efforts are making Milos Kerkez look like Roberto Carlos. The Greek left-back is having a dreadful afternoon and Fulham are getting plenty of joy out of him. We suggested there was no chance of this game finishing goalless, and it’s anomalous that we have reached 40 minutes without score. Fulham, certainly, have a sense of adventure and have been into Liverpool’s 18-yard box plenty of times. Let’s see if the picture changes before the interval.

That’s now seven goals Emi Martinez has conceded in three games since joining from Villa to supposedly solve Chelsea’s goalkeeping crisis. Martinez won’t be pleased with Hull’s second goal, here. He was beaten to a corner by Ajayi. His header hit the bar and Belloumi’s shot was deflected past him. The Hull fans are in dreamland.

This is a turn up for the books. Chelsea undone by a long ball forward, and Hato lets the ball bounce over his head, and Belloumi finishes with aplomb.

That’s now 20 Premier League games Chelsea have gone without keeping a clean sheet. What an earth was Jorrel Hato doing, letting the ball bounce over him for Belloumi? Amateur stuff at the back from the home side. It was Hull’s first meaningful attack.

Emersonn has struggled in some games so far this season, but he has just planted a header into the corner from a Davis cross.

There is a VAR check for offside... but the goal stands.

5 - Morgan Rogers is the fifth different player to score or assist in each of Chelsea's first four games of a Premier League season, after Didier Drogba (2010-11), Cesc Fàbregas (2014-15), Diego Costa (2014-15 & 2016-17), and Eden Hazard (2018-19).Famous. pic.twitter.com/0cuThzH472

A sweet strike from one of Palace’s summer signings, recruited from Union Saint Gilloise, and that is his first Palace goal. The 22-year-old Israeli came through at Maccabi Haifa. Uphill task for Gary O’Neill and Ipswich.

Austin MacPhee, Chelsea’s flamboyant set-piece coach, just motioned for Xabi Alonso to sit down when the Blues manager momentarily got up from his seat when the home side were preparing to take a corner. It seems MacPhee wears the (correct length) trousers when it comes to set pieces.

An almighty let off for Alisson and Liverpool after pass from the goalkeeper played Gravenberch into trouble, but Jacquet cleared off the line to keep the game goalless. That was Fulham’s first foray forward.

A bright start in this game and there is no chance it will end goalless (famous last words). Andoni Iraola has made three changes from the team that beat Atletico Madrid on Wednesday and it’s a pattern of his early management that he is making the kind of decisions that supporters are nodding along in approval with. Liverpool should already be one up but Alexander Isak’s shot has just drifted across the face of goal but the signs are encouraging. It could be a long afternoon for Alvaro Arbeloa.

Wow. Unbelievable double save from Forest’s Matz Sels there to keep out Victor Lindelof.

The first was the most impressive, a reflex stop after a deflection.

Morgan Rogers is the first player to score against Hull City this season. Emi Martinez launched the ball forward after claiming a corner, and Rogers’ shot from the edge of the area crept under the goalkeeper Tzolakis. He will not want to watch that one again.

We’re past five minutes and it’s the longest Chelsea have gone without scoring in the league this season. Back on Matt Crooks – one of his middle names is Rider.

Although Rogers scored in the seventh minute...so the early goals continue for Chelsea. It will be difficult for Hull now.

Twelve seconds in and the chant “where were you in Istanbul” gets a very early airing from Villa’s home fans.

That is of course a reference to Villa’s 4-0 win over Forest in the Europa League semi-final second leg last season.

The early indications are that Reece James is playing in midfield with Malo Gusto at right-back in a conventional back four.

Xabi Alonso has made an encouraging start to life as Chelsea manager. But his trousers upset me. They are three inches too short and a bit baggy above the ankle.

We are under way in the five Premier League 3pm kick-offs. Goals and further updates from around the grounds as they happen.

Some early #analysis from Matt at the Bridge, about one of Hull’s midfielders.

One player who has really shone for Villa so far this season is teenage midfielder George Hemmings.

Unai Emery has been very impressed with the academy graduate, who made his Champions League debut on Tuesday night.

There is also a big buzz around £51m signing Johan Manzambi, who is on the bench today after recovering from a knee injury.

Will we get another fast start from Chelsea today? They have scored inside the first five minutes in all three of their League games this season. Hull are yet to concede.

Dominic King writes that there were signs of promise in the relationship between Barcola, Wirtz and Isak in Liverpool’s win over Atletico Madrid, and all three forwards start against Fulham. Timothy Castagne, Fulham’s right-back will need to have his sprinting boots on against Barcola, who is grease lightning.

Cole Palmer has 15 goal involvements in his 15 Premier League games for Chelsea against newly promoted sides.9 goals ⚽6 assists 🅰️ pic.twitter.com/PJIU0YxIhQ

I’m having real fun. I’ve got a smile on face and I’m enjoying my football. Playing with players like [Palmer and Joao Pedro] inspire you to be better and make you do better and do well for the team. We are in a good moment and we want to keep it going.

Hull are really tough to beat. They have played against some good opponents and they’ve kept them out - they haven’t conceded yet. It is going to be difficult because they are really organised but we are at home and it is on us to make the game about us.

We know it is always tough against Brentford. We can expect a tight game today, definitely. We both want to win so it’ll be a nice game.

We are very excited about our first European game coming up but we haven’t really spoken about it lately because we have just spoken about this game. This is a big game and we are looking for our first three points of the season. We have been close in every game so we hope to get it today.

Unai Emery is possibly the best coach in the Premier League but has found past encounters with Oliver Glasner very uncomfortable.

Since Glasner’s arrival in English football with Crystal Palace in February 2024, he has faced Emery’s Villa seven times and never lost.

With five victories and two draws, it is an impressive record albeit with a different set of players.

Aston Villa and Forest are two teams in transition, and meet for the first time since that two-legged Europa League semi-final last season.

Villa are building a new chapter after a summer of significant change, while Forest are implementing a totally different style of play under Oliver Glasner.

Returning to Villa Park will have some bitter memories for a number of the Forest players, after that 4-0 defeat in the second leg of the Europa League.
